>>> spec = mujoco.mjspec.from_string( ... '<mujoco><worldbody><body name="d"><freejoint/><geom name="a" size="0.1"/><geom size="0.1"/></body>' ... '<geom name="b" size="0.1" pos="1 0 0"/><geom name="c" size="0.1" pos="0 0 -0.21"/></worldbody>' ... '<contact><pair geom1="a" geom2="b"/><pair geom1="a" geom2="c"/></contact></mujoco>' ... ) >>> coarse = mjwarpsim.build_coarse_spec(spec, coarseconfig(qpos_ref=np.array([[0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0]]))) >>> coarse.compile().npair # only a-c comes near 1 >>> config = coarseconfig(collide="a|c|d", condim=1, condim_geoms="d", timestep=0.01, pyramidal=true) >>> model = mjwarpsim.build_coarse_spec(spec, config).compile() >>> model.geom_contype.tolist(), model.geom_condim.tolist() # b, c, a, d's unnamed: b no longer collides ([0, 1, 1, 1], [3, 3, 3, 1]) >>> model.opt.timestep, model.opt.cone (0.01, 0) >>> config = coarseconfig(min_timeconst=0.01, min_impedance_width=0.002) >>> model = mjwarpsim.build_coarse_spec(spec, config).compile() >>> model.geom_solref[:, 0].tolist(), model.geom_solimp[:, 2].tolist() # from 0.02 and 0.001 by default ([0.02, 0.02, 0.02, 0.02], [0.002, 0.002, 0.002, 0.002]) >>> config = coarseconfig(iterations=2, ls_iterations=4, integrator="implicitfast") >>> opt = mjwarpsim.build_coarse_spec(spec, config).option >>> opt.iterations, opt.ls_iterations, opt.integrator == mujoco.mjtintegrator.mjint_implicitfast (2, 4, true)

simcontext robokit.terms class context

values a planner gives its terms for one world set (sim_context); arrays are refilled every step.

statetask robokit.terms class simresidualtask

per step, the weighted qpos error norm plus vel_weight times the qvel error norm, and optional contact terms; its residuals cover the errors, while the contact terms (penetration, missing contacts) are cost-only, so simmpc sees them and ilqroptimizer does not.

example

python
>>> import copy, mujoco >>> from robokit.helpers.sim_mpc import sim_context >>> from robokit.sim import mjwarpsim >>> model = mujoco.mjmodel.from_xml_string( ... '<mujoco><worldbody><body><freejoint/><geom size="0.1"/></body></worldbody></mujoco>' ... ) >>> data = mujoco.mjdata(model) >>> data.qpos[0] = 0.05 # 5 cm off the reference in x >>> context = sim_context(mjwarpsim(model, 1, data)) | { ... simcontext.clock: wp.array([0, 0, 1], dtype=int), ... simcontext.num_instances: 1, ... simcontext.worlds_per_instance: 1, ... } >>> qpos_ref, qvel_ref, out = np.tile(model.qpos0, (2, 1)), np.zeros((2, model.nv)), wp.zeros(2, dtype=float) >>> for i, tolerance in enumerate([0.0, 0.01]): ... term = copy.copy(statetask(qpos_ref, qvel_ref, np.ones(model.nv), pose_tolerance=tolerance)) ... term.resolve(none, context) ... term.compute_weighted_cost(none, out_cost=out[i : i + 1]) >>> assert np.allclose(out.numpy(), [0.05, 0.04])
import numpy as np import warp as wp from robokit.terms.simulation.sim_context import simcontext from robokit.terms.simulation.state_task import statetask import copy, mujoco from robokit.helpers.sim_mpc import sim_context from robokit.sim import mjwarpsim model = mujoco.mjmodel.from_xml_string( '<mujoco><worldbody><body><freejoint/><geom size="0.1"/></body></worldbody></mujoco>' ) data = mujoco.mjdata(model) data.qpos[0] = 0.05 # 5 cm off the reference in x context = sim_context(mjwarpsim(model, 1, data)) | { simcontext.clock: wp.array([0, 0, 1], dtype=int), simcontext.num_instances: 1, simcontext.worlds_per_instance: 1, } qpos_ref, qvel_ref, out = np.tile(model.qpos0, (2, 1)), np.zeros((2, model.nv)), wp.zeros(2, dtype=float) for i, tolerance in enumerate([0.0, 0.01]): term = copy.copy(statetask(qpos_ref, qvel_ref, np.ones(model.nv), pose_tolerance=tolerance)) term.resolve(none, context) term.compute_weighted_cost(none, out_cost=out[i : i + 1]) assert np.allclose(out.numpy(), [0.05, 0.04])

contacttask robokit.terms class task

reward geoms' contacts inside their target discs; penalize touches outside every allowed disc.

box, half widths (x, y), replaces each target disc with that axis-aligned box around the target; height, (low, high), rewards only contacts at those heights.

example

python
>>> context = { # one contact of geom 1 at (0, 0), 0.25 apart, at sim step 1 ... simcontext.clock: wp.array([1, 0, 1], dtype=int, device="cpu"), ... simcontext.num_instances: 1, ... simcontext.worlds_per_instance: 1, ... simcontext.geoms: ["floor", "foot"], ... simcontext.contacts: tuple( ... wp.array(x, dtype=t, device="cpu") ... for x, t in [([1], int), ([0], int), ([[0, 1]], wp.vec2i), ([0.25], float), ([[0, 0, 0]], wp.vec3)] ... ), ... } >>> far, allowed = np.ones((1, 1, 2)), np.array([[[[0.0, 0.0, 0.1]]]]) # a disc (x, y, r) around the foot >>> terms = [ ... contacttask(["foot"], np.zeros((1, 1, 2)), np.full((1, 2, 1), 0.1), weight=2.0), # radius over time ... contacttask(["foot"], far, np.zeros((1, 1)), penalty=0.5, margin=0.3), ... contacttask(["foot"], far, np.zeros((1, 1)), allowed, penalty=0.5, margin=0.3), ... contacttask(["foot"], far, np.zeros((1, 1)), weight=2.0, box=(1.0, 1.0)), # (0, 0) is in the box ... contacttask(["foot"], far, np.zeros((1, 1)), weight=2.0, box=(1.0, 1.0), height=(0.1, 1.0)), # too low ... ] >>> out = wp.zeros(5, dtype=float, device="cpu") >>> for i, term in enumerate(terms): ... term.resolve(none, context) ... term.compute_weighted_cost(none, out_cost=out[i : i + 1]) >>> assert np.allclose(out.numpy(), [-2.0 * 0.75, 0.5, 0.0, -2.0 * 0.75, 0.0])

robokit/dev: development guide development guide setup clone the repository and install the development environment with uv : shell git clone https://github.com/openrobokit/robokit cd robokit uv sync pytorch is optional. for examples that need it, pick the extra for your cuda toolkit: shell uv sync --extra pt-cu126 # cuda 12.6 uv sync --extra pt-cu118 # cuda 11.8 uv sync --extra pt-cu128 # cuda 12.8 uv sync --extra pt-cpu # cpu only see installation for other extras. git workflow work on your own branch. merge to main through a pull request with squash merge , then delete the branch. run make ci before committing; it formats, lints, type-checks and runs all tests. it defaults to pt-cu126 ; use make ci pt=pt-cpu for cpu-only pytorch. formatting, linting, and type checking use ruff for formatting and linting: shell uvx ruff check uvx ruff format use pyright for type checking: shell uv run pyright warp's stubs cannot type every kernel expression. put a needed pyright ignore on that expression only; keep host code checked. in autograd wrappers, narrow optional gradient buffers only where they are always allocated. function naming start function names with one of these verbs: solve : run an iterative optimization; may fail. compute : direct evaluation; always succeeds. build : construct objects, buffers, or kernels. get : cached lookup (build on miss). set / clear : mutate or drop state. warp kernels and functions additionally: suffix by type: *_kernel for @wp.kernel , *_func for @wp.func . verbs also include transform / integrate / accept . variant tags before the suffix, fixed order: representation ( matrix ), algorithm ( sequential / local / accum ), then backward . variable naming use the public notation : t_dst_src , t_dst_src , q_wxyz_dst_src , and q for joint positions. keep wxyz in quaternion parameter names to indicate ordering. avoid pose , tf , or similar terms, except in robokit.xform , whose conversions take tf_mat and pose7 . use t_dst_src for batched transformations, not ts_dst_src . comments and docstrings use the full-width separator for sections. use the short form for class sections and long phases inside a function. python # --- kernels ---------------------------------------------------------------- # --- build solver --- use lowercase fragments for section labels and short code comments: python # skip the normal/closest math (~2x faster) write full-sentence comments with normal capitalization and punctuation. keep proper names, acronyms and identifiers as they are. spell out words in section labels. use google-style docstrings ( args: / returns: / raises: sections) with single-backtick inline code. testing run pytest and documentation tests: shell uv run pytest uv run xdoctest robokit uv run scripts/test_docs.py markdown examples each python fence runs on its own. include imports, small sample inputs and assertions. wrap setup and checks in # docs: hide / # docs: endhide to hide them from the short view: text # docs: hide values = [1, 2, 3] # docs: endhide total = sum(values) # docs: hide assert total == 6 # docs: endhide the website shows the short view; full and copy use the complete code. scripts/test_docs.py runs every fence with xdoctest. hide # xdoctest: +skip in examples that download assets, and # xdoctest: +requires(...) in optional ones: robokit_cuda_docs=1 for cuda, robokit_body_models for body models, robokit_parahome_docs=1 for parahome. to test the website's copies, run uv run scripts/test_docs.py <robokit-website>/_page/docs/robokit . doctest give every public function a doctest: python full def quaternion_multiply( q_wxyz_1: float[torch.tensor, "... 4"], q_wxyz_2: float[torch.tensor, "... 4"] ) -> float[torch.tensor, "... 4"]: """ multiply two quaternions. example: >>> q1 = torch.tensor([0.9238795, 0.0, 0.0, 0.3826834]) >>> q2 = torch.tensor([0.9238795, 0.0, 0.0, 0.3826834]) >>> expected = torch.tensor([0.7071068, 0.0, 0.0, 0.7071068]) >>> torch.allclose(quaternion_multiply(q1, q2), expected, atol=1e-6) true """ return _quaternion_multiply(q_wxyz_1, q_wxyz_2) import torch from jaxtyping import float from robokit.xform.warp.torch_wrappers import quaternion_multiply as _quaternion_multiply def quaternion_multiply( q_wxyz_1: float[torch.tensor, "... 4"], q_wxyz_2: float[torch.tensor, "... 4"] ) -> torch.tensor([0.7071068, 0.0, 0.0, 0.7071068]) >>> torch.allclose(quaternion_multiply(q1, q2), expected, atol=1e-6) true """ return _quaternion_multiply(q_wxyz_1, q_wxyz_2) q = torch.tensor([0.9238795, 0.0, 0.0, 0.3826834]) torch.testing.assert_close(quaternion_multiply(q, q), torch.tensor([0.7071068, 0, 0, 0.7071068])) pytest tests use local fixtures. hugging face calls are blocked. to test mano pkl conversion and cpu engine parity with local body models : shell robokit_body_models="$home/.robokit/body_models" cuda_visible_devices='' \ uv run pytest tests/assets/test_body_models.py tests/smplx/test_mano_engine.py -q --no-cov group test cases into one class. compare results across implementations: python full class testquaterniontomatrix:
