task previews are under built-in-tasks/ . pages link them by relative path. gallery recordings stay in the website repository. update assets here, then run make import project=robokit src=/path/to/robokit in the website checkout, with src pointing at this branch or worktree. do not keep copies in the website source. asset authoring robot descriptions, datasets and collision configs live at openrobokit/robokit . import an asset module to use its path symbols. see built-in robots & datasets for loading assets and fetch() . layout text ~/.robokit/ ├── assets/ # extension-preserving runtime paths │ └── <pinned-commit>/ │ ├── robots/ │ │ ├── robot_description/ # urdfs and meshes │ │ │ ├── arms/ │ │ │ ├── end_effectors/ │ │ │ ├── humanoids/ │ │ │ └── assembly/ │ │ ├── robot_mj_description/ # mjcfs and mujoco assets │ │ ├── collision_spheres/ │ │ ├── contact_points/ │ │ ├── contact_avoid_points/ │ │ └── self_collision/ │ ├── datasets/ # one folder per source │ │ └── <name>/ # clips, metadata, objects/ when provided │ ├── policies/ │ └── calibration/ ├── body_models/ # user-provided, never fetched from hf │ ├── mano/ │ └── smplx/ ├── hf_cache/ # hugging face blobs and snapshots │ └── datasets--openrobokit--robokit/ │ ├── blobs/ │ └── snapshots/ └── hf_repo/ # writable authoring checkout robot files are type-major. one robot's urdf, collision spheres and contact points sit in different robots/ subdirs under the same robot name. each dataset source gets a lowercase datasets/<name>/ folder for its clips and object meshes. its access module lives in robokit.assets.datasets . robot asset naming robokit-generated files use <model>_<side>[_<modifier>...] ; directories use <model>_<side> . common modifiers, in order: glb , floating_base , no_mimic . python modules stay side-neutral. side-specific symbols end in _right or _left . add no unsuffixed aliases. variant-specific symbols use a prefix, such as arm_urdf_path and arm_rest_q . rest_q maps every actuated joint name to its rest position. arms, humanoids and end effectors expose mount_link_name and mount_coord_spec , with _right and _left on bilateral models. the link's frame is the mounting frame. the spec gives its outward and right axes and an optional mount_point_xyz , all in that frame. end effectors also expose ee_coord_spec , a handcoordinatespec or grippercoordinatespec . their mount_coord_spec , including mount_point_xyz , is derived from it. display names use <model> right or <model> left ; side-neutral assets omit the side. self-collision ignore sets scripts/geom/self_collision/generate_ignore.py writes ignore.<backend>.{yml,srdf} for one robot. run it per model and backend, into the writable checkout. capsule needs only the urdf/mjcf; sphere also needs collision spheres that cover the whole model: shell uv run scripts/geom/self_collision/generate_ignore.py <urdf> --backend capsule \ --out-dir ~/.robokit/hf_repo/robots/self_collision/<robot> --out-stem ignore uv run scripts/geom/self_collision/generate_ignore.py <urdf> --backend sphere --spheres <yaml> \ --out-dir ~/.robokit/hf_repo/robots/self_collision/<robot> --out-stem ignore expose each file as sphere_ / capsule_self_collision_ignore_path , with an mj_ prefix for mjcf variants. the fcl backend is not shipped. publishing assets keep upstream license files and copyright notices beside copied assets, including those of each assembly component. create the writable checkout, edit robokit_assets/ , then commit and push: shell uv run python -c "from robokit.assets import checkout; checkout()" cd robokit_assets git add -a && git commit -m "add <asset>" && git push git rev-parse head keep the type-major layout above. in the same robokit change, expose the path in src/robokit/assets/<kind>/<name>.py . set the pinned commit in src/robokit/assets/__init__.py to the printed hash. note checkout() clones the writable checkout to ~/.robokit/hf_repo and links it as ./robokit_assets . binary assets use git lfs. before adding a new binary extension, run git lfs track "*.<ext>" .
retargetingkit/overview: overview overview retargetingkit maps human motion to robot hands, arms, and humanoids. it combines robokit optimization with neural hand models for recorded motion and real-time teleoperation. key features one pipeline. sources produce canonical motion frames; retargeters produce robot commands; targets preview or execute them. hands and bodies. solve finger motion, wrist poses, humanoid motion, and combined body-and-hand interactions. optimization + neural. choose geometry-aware optimization or trained hand inference for the task. recorded or live. retarget clips in parallel or drive robots from vr, gloves, and motion capture. how it works flowchart lr source["`source *vr · gloves · mocap · recordings*`"] retargeter["`retargeter *optimization + neural*`"] target["`target *viser · robot hardware*`"] source -- "frame: hand · arm · body" --> retargeter retargeter -- "command: joints · base pose" --> target classdef endpoint fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#111827 classdef solver fill:#dbc8ea,stroke:#8163a1,stroke-width:2px,color:#111827 class source,target endpoint class retargeter solver component role read more source read a device or recording. sources frame represent human hand, arm, or body motion. frames retargeter map motion to a robot through optimization or neural inference. interfaces command carry robot joints and an optional base pose. commands target preview motion or command hardware. targets features hand retargeting map tracked hand motion to robot joints. geometry-aware hand retargeting refine hands against object geometry. real-time hand teleoperation drive a robot hand from live tracking. humanoid retargeting map captured body motion to humanoids. geometry-aware humanoid retargeting account for terrain and contact. real-time humanoid teleoperation drive a humanoid from live motion. full-body retargeting combine body and hand motion. geometry-aware full-body retargeting preserve scene and object interactions. real-time full-body teleoperation drive body and hands together. quick links quickstart installation framework concepts asset setup
retargetingkit/quickstart: quickstart quickstart try it without installing choose a free gpu and set cuda_visible_devices . then run the interactive hand gallery without installing retargetingkit: shell uvx --from 'retargetingkit[vis]' \ python -m retargetingkit.gallery.hand_retargeting open the viser url printed in the terminal. select a robot and motion, then play or scrub the result. replace hand_retargeting with any gallery below. each preview records that gallery's viser scene. hand_retargeting retarget tracked hands. hand_neural compare neural hand models. hand_contact refine hand-object contact. hand_object_dexmachina explore dexmachina interactions. hand_object_gigahands explore gigahands interactions. hand_object_oakink2 explore oakink2 interactions. humanoid browse motions and robot presets. humanoid_contact retarget object interactions. humanoid_terrain adapt motion to terrain. full_body_hoi retarget body and hand interactions. full_body_hsi retarget body motion in furnished scenes. to list gallery module names from an installed checkout, run uv run python -m retargetingkit.gallery . gallery data, robot models, and checkpoints download on first use; complete asset setup first. solve one humanoid retargeting problem after installing , this program maps one frame of the included bvh recording to a unitree g1 pose on cpu: python from retargetingkit.assets.sample_bvh import example_bvh from retargetingkit.retargeting.humanoid.online import humanoidretargeterconfig from retargetingkit.retargeting.humanoid.presets.g1 import g1_aligned from retargetingkit.sources.misc.human_frame_file import bodyfilesourceconfig source = bodyfilesourceconfig(example_bvh, use_ankle_as_foot_target=true).build() retargeter = humanoidretargeterconfig(g1_aligned).build("cpu") command = retargeter.solve(source.get_frame()) print(command.qpos.shape, command.base_pose.shape) # (29,) (7,) source.close() the source produces a bodyframe ; the retargeter returns g1 joint positions and a floating-base pose. more examples galleries are interactive demos. for code to copy, open a runnable script below. paths are relative to src/retargetingkit/examples . directory scripts hand_optimization 01_online.py , 02_offline.py , 03_batch.py , 04_arm.py , 05_online_batch.py , 06_dexycb_online.py hand_neural 02_batch.py humanoid 01_online.py , 02_collision.py , 03_self_collision.py , 04_offline.py , 05_batch.py , 06_online_batch.py , 07_contact.py full_body 01_hoi.py , 02_hsi.py example usage: shell uv run --extra vis src/retargetingkit/examples/humanoid/01_online.py
retargetingkit/install: installation installation retargetingkit needs python 3.10 or newer. uv pip shell uv add retargetingkit shell pip install retargetingkit from source uv pip shell uv add git+https://github.com/openrobokit/retargetingkit.git shell pip install git+https://github.com/openrobokit/retargetingkit.git to work on retargetingkit itself, clone the repository and run uv sync . see the development guide . extras extra what it adds vis browser galleries and viser previews. contact hand-object contact examples. vision-pro , pico , manus , axis live motion sources; see sources . xarm , inspire , ability physical arm and hand targets; see targets . realsense realsense camera source. rby1 , dexmate humanoid hardware connections. the pico , manus , and axis extras use wheels from a separate index: uv pip shell uv add "retargetingkit[manus]" --index https://jianglongye.github.io/torch_packages_builder shell pip install "retargetingkit[manus]" --extra-index-url https://jianglongye.github.io/torch_packages_builder see assets , then start with the quickstart .
retargetingkit/hand-optimization: hand retargeting hand retargeting hand motion on a robot assembly. hand-object contact refinement. map human hand motion to robot joint positions with robokit's online or offline optimization. start with a recorded example, then connect a manus glove or apple vision pro . how retargeting works a source supplies hand keypoints. the optimization retargeter matches them to a robot hand while respecting its joints and, when configured, object contact. online solving handles one frame at a time; offline solving optimizes a trajectory. both produce joint positions in the robot's urdf order. try a recording from the retargetingkit checkout, run: shell uv run --extra vis python -m retargetingkit.examples.hand_optimization.01_online open the viser address printed in the terminal. the example replays hand motion and shows the retargeted robot without connecting hardware. required assets download on first use. press ctrl+c to stop. use the python api build a rig's retargeter and pass it one handframe per update: python full from retargetingkit.configs.teleop.hand.manus_sharpa import right_manus_sharpa_config retargeter = right_manus_sharpa_config.retargeter.build(device) for frame in stream: # handframe: right-hand mano-21 keypoints command = retargeter.solve(frame) qpos = command.qpos # (22,), sharpa joints in urdf order import pickle import numpy as np import warp as wp from retargetingkit.assets.example_data import manus_data_right_pkl from retargetingkit.sources.frames import handframe, handpose device = "cuda:0" if wp.is_cuda_available() else "cpu" # three recorded wrist-local mano-21 frames from a right manus glove. keypoints = pickle.load(open(manus_data_right_pkl, "rb"))["keypoints"][:3] stream = [handframe({"right": handpose(points)}) for points in keypoints] from retargetingkit.configs.teleop.hand.manus_sharpa import right_manus_sharpa_config retargeter = right_manus_sharpa_config.retargeter.build(device) for frame in stream: # handframe: right-hand mano-21 keypoints command = retargeter.solve(frame) qpos = command.qpos # (22,), sharpa joints in urdf order assert qpos.shape == (22,) assert np.isfinite(qpos).all() preview live motion complete the source setup first. for a right manus glove and xhand: shell uv run --extra manus --extra vis scripts/teleop/hand.py \ manus_xhand --mode viser the live runtime defaults to cuda:0 . select an available gpu with cuda_visible_devices before launching, or pass --device cpu for optimization on cpu. optimization rig source robot hand manus_xhand manus xhand manus_sharpa manus sharpa wave visionpro_xhand vision pro xhand visionpro_sharpa vision pro sharpa wave inspect a preset's device settings with uv run scripts/teleop/hand.py manus_xhand --help . vision pro requires the vision-pro extra. connect the robot after checking motion in the viewer, configure the matching xhand or sharpa target. mode behavior viser preview only; the robot target is not opened. this is the default. real connect and command the physical hand. both command the physical hand and show viser. for example, manus_xhand --mode both --target.serial-port /dev/ttyusb0 enables xhand hardware alongside the preview. work with trajectories use the packaged examples to inspect solver construction and array shapes: module under retargetingkit.examples.hand_optimization task 01_online retarget one stream frame by frame 02_offline optimize one recorded trajectory 03_batch optimize several trajectories together 04_arm retarget an arm and hand together 05_online_batch retarget several arm-hand streams online run any module with uv run --extra vis python -m <module> . robot outputs use urdf joint order. online inputs have shape (k, 3) or (b, k, 3) , with points ordered by spec.target_names ; offline inputs add a time axis. inspect object contact browse dexycb recordings with an xarm7–xhand or xarm7–ability assembly and compare contact refinement in the viewer: shell uv run --extra vis python -m retargetingkit.gallery.hand_contact for learned inference, including the supported live manus_sharpa_neural rig, continue with neural hand retargeting .
retargetingkit/neural-hand: neural hand retargeting neural hand retargeting train a model for one robot hand, then map wrist-local mano-21 keypoints to joint positions in urdf order. curated checkpoints support allegro, sharpa wave, and xhand. how inference works the source returns a handframe ; the selected checkpoint maps its wrist-local keypoints to a qposcommand . a checkpoint belongs to one robot hand, so choose the matching hand and model before connecting a target. try a trained model run the gallery from the retargetingkit checkout: shell uv run --extra vis python -m retargetingkit.gallery.hand_neural open the printed viser address to choose a hand and checkpoint. the selected model downloads on first use and is cached. these commands default to cuda; select an available gpu with cuda_visible_devices , or use --device cpu . use the python api load a named checkpoint for its hand and pass it one handframe per update: python full from retargetingkit.retargeting.hand.neural import neuralhandassetretargeterconfig from retargetingkit.retargeting.hand.presets import hands config = neuralhandassetretargeterconfig("sharpa_motion_alignment", hands["sharpa"]) retargeter = config.build(device) for frame in stream: # handframe: right-hand mano-21 keypoints command = retargeter.solve(frame) qpos = command.qpos # (22,), sharpa joint angles import pickle import numpy as np import warp as wp from retargetingkit.assets.example_data import manus_data_right_pkl from retargetingkit.sources.frames import handframe, handpose device = "cuda:0" if wp.is_cuda_available() else "cpu" # three recorded wrist-local mano-21 frames from a right manus glove. keypoints = pickle.load(open(manus_data_right_pkl, "rb"))["keypoints"][:3] stream = [handframe({"right": handpose(points)}) for points in keypoints] from retargetingkit.retargeting.hand.neural import neuralhandassetretargeterconfig from retargetingkit.retargeting.hand.presets import hands config = neuralhandassetretargeterconfig("sharpa_motion_alignment", hands["sharpa"]) retargeter = config.build(device) for frame in stream: # handframe: right-hand mano-21 keypoints command = retargeter.solve(frame) qpos = command.qpos # (22,), sharpa joint angles assert qpos.shape == (22,) assert np.isfinite(qpos).all() with a configured manus glove , preview live sharpa inference: shell uv run --extra manus --extra vis scripts/teleop/hand.py \ manus_sharpa_neural --mode viser this preset loads sharpa_motion_alignment_contact_inhand . set --mode real or --mode both to connect and command a physical sharpa hand . train a recipe five training recipes live in scripts/teleop/neural_hand/configs/training/ : hand recipe filename allegro allegro_motion_alignment.yaml xhand xhand_motion_alignment.yaml sharpa sharpa_motion_alignment.yaml sharpa with contact data sharpa_motion_alignment_contact.yaml sharpa with in-hand contact data sharpa_motion_alignment_contact_inhand.yaml for example: shell uv run scripts/teleop/neural_hand/train.py \ scripts/teleop/neural_hand/configs/training/xhand_motion_alignment.yaml the yaml selects named motion and calibration assets, loss weights, and an output directory. training writes train.yaml with data provenance and weights.pt to ik_model/xhand_motion_alignment/ for this recipe. the output directory must not already exist; choose a new output path for another run. record your own motion record the right manus glove at 30 hz: shell uv run --extra manus --extra vis scripts/teleop/neural_hand/record_motion.py \ --output motion.npz press enter to start, then enter again to stop and save. add --no-viz to record without a viewer. to use this recording for training, register it as a named asset in retargetingkit.assets.calib and reference that name under data.unsupervised in your yaml. replay the recording through your trained model: shell uv run --extra vis scripts/teleop/neural_hand/visualize.py xhand \ --checkpoints ik_model/xhand_motion_alignment --data motion.npz add contact supervision the sharpa contact workflow generates candidate ycb grasps, then captures matching human poses: shell uv run --extra contact scripts/teleop/neural_hand/contact_generate.py \ scripts/teleop/neural_hand/configs/contact/sharpa_ycb_contact.yaml uv run --extra contact --extra manus --extra vis \ scripts/teleop/neural_hand/contact_capture.py \ --specs sharpa_grasp.npz --output training_data.npz use the capture viewer to record, skip, and save samples. register the result as a calibration asset and reference it under data.contact in a training yaml. for paired human/robot measurements, record_pairs.py supports manus and sharpa. it starts in neural control mode and commands the physical hand; t toggles teaching mode, c captures a pair, and q saves and exits.
retargetingkit/arm-retargeting: arm retargeting arm retargeting map a tracked wrist to an xarm6 or xarm7 end effector. the arm solver uses robokit inverse kinematics with position, orientation, joint-limit, and smoothness terms. how retargeting works the source reports wrist poses in an armframe . calibration establishes the robot's home pose; inverse kinematics then maps relative wrist motion to a joint-position command for each arm. preview one arm complete vision pro setup , then run: shell uv run --extra vision-pro scripts/teleop/arm.py \ visionpro_xarm7 --mode viser --device cpu \ --source.ip <vision_pro_ip> open the viser url printed in the terminal. visionpro_xarm6 selects xarm6; visionpro_dual_xarm7 controls two independent arms. use the python api build the rig's right-arm retargeter and pass it one armframe per update: python full from retargetingkit.configs.teleop.arm.visionpro_xarm7 import right_visionpro_xarm7_config retargeter = right_visionpro_xarm7_config.retargeters["right"].build(device) for frame in stream: # armframe: world-frame wrist [x, y, z, qw, qx, qy, qz] command = retargeter.solve(frame) qpos = command.qpos # (7,), xarm7 joint positions import numpy as np import warp as wp from retargetingkit.sources.frames import armframe device = "cuda:0" if wp.is_cuda_available() else "cpu" # a right wrist moving 10 cm forward. stream = [armframe({"right": np.array([x, -0.2, 1.1, 1, 0, 0, 0], dtype=np.float32)}) for x in (0.0, 0.05, 0.1)] from retargetingkit.configs.teleop.arm.visionpro_xarm7 import right_visionpro_xarm7_config retargeter = right_visionpro_xarm7_config.retargeters["right"].build(device) for frame in stream: # armframe: world-frame wrist [x, y, z, qw, qx, qy, qz] command = retargeter.solve(frame) qpos = command.qpos # (7,), xarm7 joint positions assert qpos.shape == (7,) assert np.isfinite(qpos).all() the first frame is the calibration origin, so it returns the home pose. retarget an arm and hand optimize the arm and fingers from each synchronized armhandframe . the wrist pose is in world coordinates; hand keypoints are wrist-local. this example builds only the solvers and needs no tracking device or robot connection. python full from retargetingkit.configs.teleop.arm_hand.visionpro_xarm7_xhand import right_visionpro_xarm7_xhand_config config = right_visionpro_xarm7_xhand_config arm = config.arm_retargeters["right"].build(device) hand = config.hand_retargeters["right"].build(device) for frame in stream: # armhandframe: synchronized wrist and finger poses arm_qpos = arm.solve(frame.arm).qpos # (7,), xarm7 joints hand_qpos = hand.solve(frame.hand).qpos # (12,), xhand joints import pickle import numpy as np import warp as wp from retargetingkit.assets.example_data import manus_data_right_pkl from retargetingkit.sources.frames import armframe, armhandframe, handframe, handpose device = "cuda:0" if wp.is_cuda_available() else "cpu" keypoints = pickle.load(open(manus_data_right_pkl, "rb"))["keypoints"][:3] # recorded finger poses paired with a wrist moving 10 cm forward. stream = [ armhandframe( armframe({"right": np.array([0.05 * i, -0.2, 1.1, 1, 0, 0, 0], dtype=np.float32)}), handframe({"right": handpose(points)}), ) for i, points in enumerate(keypoints) ] from retargetingkit.configs.teleop.arm_hand.visionpro_xarm7_xhand import right_visionpro_xarm7_xhand_config config = right_visionpro_xarm7_xhand_config arm = config.arm_retargeters["right"].build(device) hand = config.hand_retargeters["right"].build(device) for frame in stream: # armhandframe: synchronized wrist and finger poses arm_qpos = arm.solve(frame.arm).qpos # (7,), xarm7 joints hand_qpos = hand.solve(frame.hand).qpos # (12,), xhand joints assert arm_qpos.shape == (7,) assert hand_qpos.shape == (12,) assert np.isfinite(arm_qpos).all() assert np.isfinite(hand_qpos).all() calibration and motion the first tracked wrist pose becomes the calibration origin and maps to the robot's configured home pose. wrist movement is then applied relative to that origin. override for the right arm effect default --retargeters.right.translation-scale scale wrist translation 1.5 --retargeters.right.ee-gain blend each new end-effector pose with the previous pose 1.0 a smaller gain smooths movement more. use visionpro_xarm7 --help for all settings. arm-hand rigs use the prefix --arm-retargeters.right instead. connect a robot use the xarm guide for sdk installation, network setup, and hardware mode. at startup, hardware mode moves each arm to its model-specific home pose. to move fingers along with the wrist, choose a supported assembly on the vision pro page . quest controller teleoperation has its own standalone workflow and button calibration.
retargetingkit/humanoid-retargeting: humanoid retargeting humanoid retargeting human motion mapped to a humanoid. humanoid motion on terrain. map recorded or live body motion to g1 at 50 hz. the runtime sends robot root pose and joint positions to its configured targets; the sonic target derives joint velocities for whole-body control. how retargeting works a body source returns named joint poses in a bodyframe . the humanoid retargeter maps them to g1 links and solves a base pose plus joint positions. a viser target displays the command; a sonic target publishes it for whole-body control. preview recorded motion start with the packaged example, which opens a viser preview without a sonic publisher: shell uv run --extra vis python -m retargetingkit.examples.humanoid.01_online open the printed viewer address. required assets download on first use; press ctrl+c to stop. use the python api build the g1 retargeter and pass it one bodyframe per update: python full from retargetingkit.retargeting.humanoid.online import humanoidretargeterconfig from retargetingkit.retargeting.humanoid.presets.g1 import g1_aligned retargeter = humanoidretargeterconfig(g1_aligned).build(device) command = retargeter.solve(frame) # bodyframe: named world-frame joint poses base_pose = command.base_pose # (7,), [x, y, z, qw, qx, qy, qz] qpos = command.qpos # (29,), g1 joints in urdf order import numpy as np import warp as wp from retargetingkit.assets.sample_bvh import example_bvh from retargetingkit.sources.misc.human_frame_file import bodyfilesourceconfig device = "cuda:0" if wp.is_cuda_available() else "cpu" source = bodyfilesourceconfig(example_bvh, use_ankle_as_foot_target=true).build() frame = source.get_frame() from retargetingkit.retargeting.humanoid.online import humanoidretargeterconfig from retargetingkit.retargeting.humanoid.presets.g1 import g1_aligned retargeter = humanoidretargeterconfig(g1_aligned).build(device) command = retargeter.solve(frame) # bodyframe: named world-frame joint poses base_pose = command.base_pose # (7,), [x, y, z, qw, qx, qy, qz] qpos = command.qpos # (29,), g1 joints in urdf order assert base_pose.shape == (7,) assert qpos.shape == (29,) assert np.isfinite(qpos).all() source.close() publish to sonic the bundled bvh preset needs no tracking device: shell uv run --extra vis scripts/teleop/humanoid.py bvh_g1_sonic_viser every named humanoid preset publishes to sonic on port 5556 . the _viser suffix adds visualization of the same motion; it does not disable sonic. run a single publisher on that port. the live runtime defaults to cuda:0 ; select an available gpu with cuda_visible_devices , or set --device cpu . override a recording and performer height: shell uv run --extra vis scripts/teleop/humanoid.py bvh_g1_sonic_viser \ --source.path /path/to/motion.bvh --source.human-height 1.80 choose a live source complete axis studio or pico setup before starting its rig. shell uv run --extra axis --extra vis scripts/teleop/humanoid.py \ axisstudio_g1_sonic_viser --source.port 7012 --source.human-height 1.75 uv run --extra pico --extra vis scripts/teleop/humanoid.py \ pico_g1_sonic_viser --source.no-use-ankle-as-foot-target the pico override uses tracked foot poses instead of substituting ankle poses. for a pico recording, use picofile_g1_sonic_viser --source.path /path/to/recording.npz . remove _viser from these preset names to publish without a viewer. use uv run scripts/teleop/humanoid.py <rig> --help to inspect all overrides. control both inspire hands this combined rig opens one pico connection, publishes g1 motion to sonic, and connects both physical inspire hands. it has no preview mode. shell uv run --extra pico --extra inspire scripts/teleop/humanoid_hand.py \ pico_g1_inspire --source.no-use-ankle-as-foot-target \ --left-hand.serial-port /dev/ttyusb0 \ --right-hand.serial-port /dev/ttyusb1 b toggles the right hand between open and closed; y toggles the left. these are preset poses, not continuous finger tracking. see inspire hand for the serial connection. run g1 in simulation configure the deployment checkout described in g1 and sonic , then start a sonic rig and launch: shell bash scripts/tools/launch_sonic_sim.sh the launcher opens mujoco and deployment in a tmux session. in the deployment pane, press ] , then enter , to start the policy. the g1 target guide also covers connection to a real robot.
retargetingkit/full-body: full-body retargeting full-body retargeting body, hand, and object interaction. body and hand motion in a furnished scene. retarget body motion, articulated fingers, and object interaction together to a g1 with inspire hands. retargetingkit loads saga or parahome clips; robokit solves the robot motion and object poses. how retargeting works each clip supplies body motion, finger motion, and interaction geometry. the body solver tracks human poses on g1; hand solvers track the fingers; grasp and scene terms keep the combined motion aligned with objects. retarget one object interaction run the saga example from the retargetingkit checkout: shell uv run --extra vis python -m retargetingkit.examples.full_body.01_hoi the default clip contains a body, captured right-hand motion, and one object. after solving, open the printed viser address to play or scrub the result. press ctrl+c to stop. the example chooses cuda when available and otherwise uses cpu. pass --npz /path/to/clip.npz for a local saga fullgrasppose recording. the example still fetches its saga asset bundle, including object meshes. retarget an indoor interaction parahome adds bimanual interaction and a furnished scene. list the available intervals in a sequence: shell uv run --extra vis python -m retargetingkit.examples.full_body.02_hsi \ --sequence s1 --list select an interval from that list: shell uv run --extra vis python -m retargetingkit.examples.full_body.02_hsi \ --sequence s1 --index 7 --scene_clearance --scene_clearance adjusts body placement to reduce penetration into furniture. use --no_scene to omit the room, or --data_root /path/to/parahome/data to provide local parahome data. browse more clips shell uv run --extra vis python -m retargetingkit.gallery.full_body_hoi uv run --extra vis python -m retargetingkit.gallery.full_body_hsi choose a subject or sequence, then a clip in the viewer. by default, both galleries use captured finger poses and contact refinement. add --grasp to optimize and hold grasps over contact intervals. the parahome gallery also exposes scene clearance in its viewer. both galleries accept --max_frames 60 --headless to solve a shorter selection and exit without opening a viewer. dataset and model assets download on first use; gallery startup can fetch more than the selected clip. these workflows produce motion for inspection. for live g1 control, follow humanoid teleoperation .
retargetingkit/teleoperation: teleoperation teleoperation dexterous hand control. humanoid motion control. a named rig connects a source, retargeter, and target in one command. choose the flow that matches the motion you want to control, then complete the linked device setup. choose a flow flow motion source robot output hand.py manus or vision pro one robot hand arm.py vision pro one or two xarms arm_hand.py vision pro synchronized arms and hands humanoid.py bvh, axis studio , pico , or a pico recording g1 motion through sonic, with optional viser humanoid_hand.py pico body motion and buttons g1 plus two physical inspire hands quest 3 , realsense , and zed have standalone device scripts. they are not inputs to these named rigs. select a rig list the available rigs, then inspect a selected rig's settings: shell uv run scripts/teleop/hand.py --help uv run scripts/teleop/hand.py manus_xhand --help the first command lists rigs; the second shows the selected rig's fields and defaults. install the source's dependencies before running it; each device page provides a complete command. override settings configuration fields become dotted options. for example, replay a vision pro recording at its original rate and scale wrist movement: shell uv run --extra vision-pro scripts/teleop/arm.py \ visionpro_xarm7 --mode viser --device cpu \ --source.recording-path data/vision_pro.pkl \ --source.recording-fps 50 \ --retargeters.right.translation-scale 0.5 create the recording with the vision pro recorder first. recording files do not store frame rate, so pass the rate used when capturing. field family example source --source.ip , --source.recording-path arm connection --arms.right.ip arm solver in arm.py --retargeters.right.translation-scale arm solver in arm_hand.py --arm-retargeters.right.translation-scale humanoid target tuple --targets.0.port the fields available depend on the selected rig. boolean switches may use a --no- form; pico's foot mapping uses --source.no-use-ankle-as-foot-target . choose the output hand , arm , and arm_hand default to viser : mode output --mode viser browser preview --mode real physical robot --mode both physical robot and browser preview humanoid flows choose targets through the rig. a *_sonic_viser rig publishes sonic commands and displays the same motion in viser. the viewer works without a sonic receiver. humanoid_hand opens physical inspire hands and has no preview mode. sonic runs as a separate receiver. see g1 / sonic for sender and receiver settings, simulation, and deployment. start with humanoid teleoperation for body motion, or quickstart for a recording that needs no hardware. use the python api a rig is a source, a retargeter, and targets. this loop runs the bvh rig without a tracking device or robot: sonic publishes commands whether or not a receiver is running. python full from retargetingkit.configs.teleop.humanoid.bvh_g1_sonic import bvh_g1_sonic_config config = bvh_g1_sonic_config source = config.source.build() retargeter = config.retargeter.build(device) targets = [target_config.build() for target_config in config.targets] while true: frame = source.get_frame() if frame is not none: command = retargeter.solve(frame) for target in targets: target.set_command(command) import numpy as np import warp as wp device = "cuda:0" if wp.is_cuda_available() else "cpu" from retargetingkit.configs.teleop.humanoid.bvh_g1_sonic import bvh_g1_sonic_config config = bvh_g1_sonic_config source = config.source.build() retargeter = config.retargeter.build(device) targets = [target_config.build() for target_config in config.targets] while true: frame = source.get_frame() if frame is not none: command = retargeter.solve(frame) for target in targets: target.set_command(command) break assert command.qpos.shape == (29,) assert np.isfinite(command.qpos).all() for target in targets: target.close() source.close()
retargetingkit/ref-assets: assets assets recordings, checkpoints, and robot models download on first use. importing retargetingkit alone downloads nothing. cache asset source cache recordings, calibration, training data openrobokit/retargetingkit ~/.retargetingkit/assets/<revision>/ neural checkpoints same dataset, models/ik_model/ inside the same revision cache robot urdfs, meshes, collision and contact data robokit assets ~/.robokit/assets/<revision>/ mano / smpl-x body models local model files robokit_body_models or ~/.robokit/body_models/ ycb meshes ycb benchmark s3 ~/.retargetingkit/ycb/ resolve an asset use named accessors so examples and applications share the same data: python from retargetingkit.assets import calib, neural_hand, sample_bvh calibration = calib.get("manus_calib") checkpoint = neural_hand.get("sharpa_motion_alignment_contact_inhand") motion = sample_bvh.example_bvh robot models come from robokit: python from robokit.assets.robots.end_effectors import sharpa_hand urdf = sharpa_hand.urdf_path_right pinned revision retargetingkit.assets.revision pins the dataset commit; accessors call robokit.assets.fetch with it, the dataset id, and ~/.retargetingkit . bump the pin after publishing new data. to download again, delete the matching ~/.retargetingkit/assets/<revision>/.done/ marker.
retargetingkit/pipeline:
pipeline pipeline retargetingkit connects a motion source, a retargeter, and one or more targets. robokit provides the robot models and optimization tools used by the solvers. flowchart td acctitle: retargetingkit framework accdescr: sources provide hand, arm, or body frames. hand optimization, neural hand inference, and arm ik produce joint commands. humanoid retargeting produces a base pose and joint command. targets display the motion or send it to robot hardware and sonic. source["sources
vr · gloves · mocap · recordings"] hand["handframe
mano-21 keypoints"] arm["armframe
world wrist poses"] body["bodyframe
named joint poses"] opt["hand
optimization"] neural["neural hand
inference"] ik["arm ik"] humanoid["humanoid
retargeting"] joints["qposcommand
joint positions"] base["baseposeqposcommand
base pose + joints"] robot["hand / arm targets
hardware · viser"] body_target["humanoid targets
viser · sonic transport"] source --> hand source --> arm source --> body hand --> opt hand --> neural arm --> ik body --> humanoid opt --> joints neural --> joints ik --> joints humanoid --> base joints --> robot base --> body_target class source framework-source on narrow screens, scroll horizontally to read the full diagram. armhandframe synchronizes wrist and finger observations from one source; the runtime sends its arm and hand frames through their respective solvers. sonic forwards humanoid commands to a separate control process for simulation or g1 hardware. three stages stage responsibility examples source convert device data or a recording into a canonical frame vision pro, manus, pico, bvh retargeter map human motion to robot joints arm ik, hand optimization, neural hand, humanoid target display or send the result viser, robot hardware, sonic transport a named rig supplies the matching source, solver, robot, and connection settings. the runtime builds them and runs the control loop. start with a named rig for a complete workflow. the diagram covers the canonical retargeting paths. quest 3 has a standalone controller workflow. the pico body-and-hands rig adds b/y button commands for inspire hand opening and closing alongside the body retargeter. shared data frames describe human motion. commands describe a single solved robot pose. the source handles device axes and joint ordering before a retargeter receives the frame. hands use wrist-local mano-21 keypoints; arms use world-frame wrist poses; bodies use named joint poses in a z-up world frame. see canonical frames for shapes and units. one loop for an initialized hand source, matching retargeter, and joint-position target: python frame = source.get_frame() if frame is not none: command = retargeter.solve(frame) target.set_qpos(command.qpos) humanoid runtimes call target.set_command(command) so the target receives the base pose together with the joints. the runtime also owns startup and cleanup; the snippet shows only one update. see interfaces to build a custom pipeline, or robokit's robot model for the underlying kinematics.
retargetingkit/frames: canonical frames canonical frames source adapters convert native device data into a shared format. solvers receive positions in meters, scalar-first quaternions, and explicit joint names. units and poses value convention position meters robot joint position radians, in actuated urdf order quaternion (qw, qx, qy, qz) pose (x, y, z, qw, qx, qy, qz) body coordinates right-handed z-up world frame canonical poses have shape (7,) . native device matrices and quaternion orders are converted inside each source adapter. human motion frame content handframe hands : side → wrist-local handpose armframe wrists : side → world-frame (7,) pose armhandframe synchronized arm and hand frames bodyframe joint_names , (j, 7) world poses, human_height sides are "left" and "right" . a frame can contain one available hand or both; check the requested side before consuming it. body joint names travel with the data so the solver can select the joints it needs. hand keypoints handpose.positions contains 21 wrist-local mano-21 points. it also carries joint orientations, a valid-point mask, and joint names. python import numpy as np from retargetingkit.sources.frames import handframe, handpose, mano21 positions = np.zeros((21, 3), dtype=np.float32) # shape example frame = handframe({"right": handpose(positions)}) frame.hands["right"].positions.shape # (21, 3) mano21.wrist, mano21.index_tip # 0, 8 mano21.thumb_tip, mano21.pinky_tip # 4, 20 replace the zero array with tracked keypoints before solving. see the frame api for all fields and defaults. robot output qposcommand carries (q,) joint positions. baseposeqposcommand adds a (7,) floating-base world pose. neither type includes a time or batch dimension; those belong to recordings and lower-level solver apis.
retargetingkit/protocols: interfaces interfaces each pipeline stage has a runtime interface and a configuration object that builds it. named rigs compose those configurations for a supported source and robot. contracts configuration builds runtime method sourceconfig source get_frame() returns a frame, or none before data arrives retargeterconfig retargeter solve(frame) returns a robot command targetconfig target set_qpos(qpos) or set_command(command) , depending on the target call source_config.build() and target_config.build() to start those components. retargeter_config.build(device) constructs and warms up the solver on the selected device. match the frame and command retargeter input output optimizationhandretargeter handframe qposcommand neuralhandretargeter handframe qposcommand armretargeter armframe qposcommand humanoidretargeter bodyframe baseposeqposcommand target declares both update methods, but concrete targets implement the methods they support. use the method expected by the selected runtime; passing only joints to a humanoid target would lose its base pose. lifecycle a runtime builds the components, reads frames, solves, and updates its targets. it calls close() on sources and targets when stopping. see teleoperation for entrypoints and overrides, and commands and targets for the api contracts.
retargetingkit/quest3: quest 3 quest 3 sources use quest 3 controllers to move one or two xarm6 or xarm7 end effectors. tracking comes through nvidia isaac teleop and cloudxr. the standalone playground supports a viser preview, controller calibration, and hardware control. connect cloudxr from the retargetingkit repository, install the playground dependencies and isaac teleop: shell uv sync --extra vis --extra xarm uv pip install "isaacteleop[cloudxr,retargeters]~=1.0.0" \ --extra-index-url https://pypi.nvidia.com start cloudxr, then load its environment in the terminal used for teleoperation: shell uv run --no-sync python -m isaacteleop.cloudxr --accept-eula . ~/.cloudxr/run/cloudxr.env the commands on this page use --no-sync to keep the installed isaac teleop environment. if a firewall is active, allow the cloudxr ports: shell sudo ufw allow 47998/udp sudo ufw allow 49100,48322/tcp open the isaac teleop webxr client in the headset browser. enter the workstation ip, accept its generated certificate, and select connect , then play . check tracking shell uv run --no-sync python scripts/sources/quest3/stream.py --side both move each controller and check that its position and orientation change. output includes xyz position and a quaternion in wxyz order; invalid means that controller is not tracked. use --side right or --side left to inspect one controller. preview an arm shell uv run --no-sync python scripts/sources/quest3/teleop.py \ --mode single --single-side right --visualize open http://localhost:8080 . align the controller with the displayed end effector, then press b to calibrate and start following your motion. the default translation scale is 0.50 . controller action right left calibrate; then pause or resume b y return to the calibrated pose a x connect xarm hardware run a single xarm7: shell uv run --no-sync python scripts/sources/quest3/teleop.py \ --mode single --single-side right \ --arm-ip <xarm_ip> --translation-scale 0.50 for two arms, set both xarm ips: shell uv run --no-sync python scripts/sources/quest3/teleop.py \ --mode bimanual \ --right-xarm-ip <right_ip> --left-xarm-ip <left_ip> \ --translation-scale 0.50 use --arm xarm6 to select xarm6. each arm moves to its home pose during startup; calibrate its controller afterward. press ctrl-c to stop. quest uses this standalone script rather than a named rig under scripts/teleop/ . keep the headset awake for long sessions, enable developer mode, connect sidequest over usb, and disable the proximity sensor in device settings & tools .
retargetingkit/vision-pro: apple vision pro apple vision pro sources stream head, wrist, and finger tracking from apple vision pro with avp_stream . retargetingkit can drive robot hands, robot arms, or synchronized arm-and-hand assemblies, and replay the same tracking from a recording. motion runtime example rig fingers scripts/teleop/hand.py visionpro_sharpa wrists scripts/teleop/arm.py visionpro_xarm7 wrists and fingers scripts/teleop/arm_hand.py visionpro_xarm7_xhand connect the headset connect the workstation and vision pro to the same wi-fi network. open tracking streamer on vision pro. note its ip address and select start . use that address as <vision_pro_ip> below. install the source dependencies from the retargetingkit repository: shell uv sync --extra vision-pro check the live stream: shell uv run --extra vision-pro scripts/sources/vision_pro/stream.py \ --ip <vision_pro_ip> the terminal prints head position and left/right pinch distances. move your head and pinch each hand to check the values. preview retargeting run a right xarm7 with xhand in viser: shell cuda_visible_devices=<free_gpu> uv run --extra vision-pro \ scripts/teleop/arm_hand.py visionpro_xarm7_xhand \ --source.ip <vision_pro_ip> --mode viser open http://localhost:8080 . the first tracked wrist frame becomes the calibration origin and maps to the arm's home pose. finger motion drives the robot hand. for arm-only or hand-only retargeting: shell cuda_visible_devices=<free_gpu> uv run --extra vision-pro \ scripts/teleop/arm.py visionpro_xarm7 --source.ip <vision_pro_ip> cuda_visible_devices=<free_gpu> uv run --extra vision-pro \ scripts/teleop/hand.py visionpro_sharpa --source.ip <vision_pro_ip> the arm runtime also offers visionpro_xarm6 and visionpro_dual_xarm7 . the hand runtime offers visionpro_xhand and visionpro_sharpa . all default to viser. connect hardware use --mode both to send the same targets to hardware and viser: shell cuda_visible_devices=<free_gpu> uv run --extra vision-pro --extra xarm \ scripts/teleop/arm_hand.py visionpro_xarm7_xhand \ --source.ip <vision_pro_ip> --mode both \ --arms.right.ip <xarm_ip> \ --hands.right.serial-port /dev/ttyusbx each arm moves to its model-specific home pose at startup. hold the wrist at the desired tracking origin when the first frame is read. use --mode real for hardware only; press ctrl-c to stop. assembly named rig hand connection xarm7 + xhand visionpro_xarm7_xhand , visionpro_dual_xarm7_xhand --hands.right.serial-port xarm7 + ability hand visionpro_xarm7_ability --hands.right.port ; add --extra ability xarm7 + inspire hand visionpro_xarm7_inspire --hands.right.serial-port ; add --extra inspire xarm7 + sharpa wave visionpro_xarm7_sharpa --hands.right.device-sn xarm6 + sharpa wave visionpro_xarm6_sharpa --hands.right.device-sn single-arm presets use the right side. for the dual xhand rig, also set --arms.left.ip and --hands.left.serial-port . sharpa uses the first discovered hand when its device serial number is unset. to tune arm-and-hand motion, use --arm-retargeters.right.translation-scale for wrist translation and --arm-retargeters.right.ee-gain for pose smoothing. the arm-only runtime uses --retargeters.right.translation-scale and --retargeters.right.ee-gain . record and replay record 15 seconds at a requested 50 hz: shell uv run --extra vision-pro scripts/sources/vision_pro/record.py \ --ip <vision_pro_ip> --duration 15 --rate 50 \ --output data/vision_pro.pkl replay with the original rate: shell cuda_visible_devices=<free_gpu> uv run --extra vision-pro \ scripts/teleop/arm.py visionpro_xarm7 \ --source.recording-path data/vision_pro.pkl \ --source.recording-fps 50 the pickle contains tracking dictionaries without timestamps or frame-rate metadata. always set --source.recording-fps to the recording rate. playback holds the final frame when it reaches the end. to inspect the recorded skeleton directly: shell uv run --extra vision-pro scripts/sources/vision_pro/visualize.py \ --recording data/vision_pro.pkl this viewer and stream.py --recording <file> use the device api's fixed default of 20 hz, so a 50 hz recording plays more slowly. tracking format the validated avp_stream 2.51 format uses finite float64 values. translations are in meters and wrist roll is in radians. field shape coordinate frame head (1, 4, 4) world left_wrist , right_wrist (1, 4, 4) world left_fingers , right_fingers (25, 4, 4) wrist-local left_arm , right_arm (25, 4, 4) or (27, 4, 4) wrist-local; optional two forearm joints left_pinch_distance , right_pinch_distance scalar thumb-tip to index-tip distance left_wrist_roll , right_wrist_roll scalar wrist roll the streamer converts world poses from y-up to right-handed z-up: x'=x , y'=-z , z'=y . finger and arm matrices stay wrist-local. the 25-joint order is wrist, four thumb joints, then five joints each for index, middle, ring, and little fingers. the optional final two arm joints are forearmwrist and forearmarm .
retargetingkit/pico: pico pico sources use pico full-body tracking through xrobotoolkit to retarget a 24-joint body to unitree g1. record sessions for offline replay, or use controller buttons to open and close two inspire hands alongside body motion. picosource converts the sdk's y-up poses to a canonical z-up bodyframe . the combined body-and-hands runtime uses b and y buttons for the hands. connect xrobotoolkit install xrobotoolkit pc service , then install the pinned python sdk from the retargetingkit repository: shell uv sync --extra pico start one foreground service and leave its terminal open. for the standard /opt/apps/roboticsservice installation: shell cd /opt/apps/roboticsservice env \ ld_library_path=/opt/apps/roboticsservice:/opt/apps/roboticsservice/lib:/opt/apps/roboticsservice/sdk/x64 \ qt_plugin_path=/opt/apps/roboticsservice/plugins \ qt_qml_path=/opt/apps/roboticsservice/qml \ ./roboticsserviceprocess connect the workstation and pico to the same wi-fi. in the headset's xrobotoolkit app, enter the workstation's wi-fi ipv4 address under pc service , select reconnect once, and apply these settings: setting value head, controller, hand checked mode fullbody high-acc unchecked num 2 send checked switch w/ a button unchecked data collection: tracking, vision unchecked network status should show working . any ip shown in a reference image is an example; enter your workstation's address. check body tracking in a second terminal, return to the retargetingkit repository and run: shell uv run --extra pico scripts/sources/pico/smoke_test.py --duration 5 move your body during the test. it prints pelvis motion and a final 24-joint snapshot. if all poses remain frozen, fully close xrobotoolkit, recalibrate both trackers in the pico motion tracker app, check that its avatar moves, and reopen xrobotoolkit. preview g1 shell cuda_visible_devices=<free_gpu> uv run --extra pico --extra vis \ scripts/teleop/humanoid.py pico_g1_sonic_viser \ --source.no-use-ankle-as-foot-target --device cuda:0 open http://localhost:8080 to see g1 follow your motion. this rig also publishes to sonic, but the preview runs without a sonic process or physical robot hands. keep --source.no-use-ankle-as-foot-target : the pico g1 profile is calibrated for pico's separate foot joints, while the named presets still default to ankle targets. set --source.human-height to the user's height in meters; the default is 1.75 . record and replay record a 15-second body session: shell uv run --extra pico scripts/sources/pico/record.py \ --duration 15 --rate 50 --out pico_recording.npz replay it without a headset: shell cuda_visible_devices=<free_gpu> uv run --extra vis \ scripts/teleop/humanoid.py picofile_g1_sonic_viser \ --source.path pico_recording.npz \ --source.no-use-ankle-as-foot-target the npz stores raw poses as (n, 24, 7) float32 , timestamps_s as seconds since recording start, and json metadata with measured frame rate and joint names. control body and hands for g1 with two connected inspire hands: shell cuda_visible_devices=<free_gpu> uv run --extra pico --extra inspire \ scripts/teleop/humanoid_hand.py pico_g1_inspire \ --source.no-use-ankle-as-foot-target \ --left-hand.serial-port <left_port> \ --right-hand.serial-port <right_port> press b to toggle the right hand or y to toggle the left hand between open and closed. this runtime uses button commands, not the pico hand skeleton. it publishes body commands to sonic; see humanoid teleoperation for simulation and g1 deployment. press ctrl-c to stop. tracking format the validated setup is pico 4 ultra with xrobotoolkit app 1.1.1, pc service 1.0.0, and python sdk 1.0.2. the wrapper converts arrays to finite float32 values. data shape format headset or controller pose (7,) [x, y, z, qx, qy, qz, qw] ; y-up world, meters body poses (24, 7) 24 smpl joints; same pose format body velocity or acceleration (24, 6) linear xyz followed by angular xyz active hand poses (27, 7) 27 joints per hand joystick (2,) x/y values motion tracker pose (7,) per tracker available in object-tracking mode fullbody mode sends the inferred body skeleton rather than raw motion tracker poses. the sdk device timestamp is an integer count of nanoseconds.
retargetingkit/manus: manus manus sources use manus gloves for hand tracking and optimization-based retargeting to xhand or sharpa wave. manussource converts each 25-node glove skeleton to a wrist-local mano-21 handframe . connect the gloves connect the gloves through the manus host software, then install the sdk runtime and viewer from the retargetingkit repository: shell uv sync --extra manus --extra vis preview both raw skeletons: shell uv run --extra manus --extra vis \ scripts/sources/manus/visualize_keypoints.py --side both open http://localhost:8080 and flex each hand to check its 25-node skeleton. the utility detects sides from glove metadata. if detection is ambiguous, pass --manus-left-id or --manus-right-id with a decimal or 0x glove id. preview retargeting shell cuda_visible_devices=<free_gpu> uv run --extra manus --extra vis \ scripts/teleop/hand.py manus_xhand --mode viser use manus_sharpa for sharpa wave. these named rigs use online optimization and default to the right hand. select --mode both for hardware plus viser or --mode real for hardware only. set --target.serial-port for xhand or --target.device-sn for sharpa. manus currently supplies hand motion only and is not a source for humanoid_hand.py . record poses capture one frame per enter press; type q and press enter to save and finish: shell uv run --extra manus --extra vis scripts/sources/manus/record_glove.py \ --hand right --output recording.npz for a finite continuous recording, set the frame count and rate: shell uv run --extra manus --extra vis scripts/sources/manus/record_glove.py \ --hand right --no-viz --frames 300 --rate 30 \ --output manus_recording.npz use --hand left or --hand both to change the recorded sides. the preview applies glove calibration; the npz preserves raw sdk positions and rotations. recording format every field begins with left_ or right_ for its saved side. positions are meters in the sdk's requested right-handed, z-up coordinate system viewed along x ( unitscale=1.0 ). field suffix shape dtype meaning positions (n, 25, 3) float32 raw node positions rotations (n, 25, 4) float32 raw quaternions in xyzw order publish_time (n,) uint64 compressed sdk timestamp recv_ns (n,) int64 host monotonic time at callback receipt timestamps (n,) float64 seconds since recording start glove_id (n,) uint32 hardware glove id side_code (n,) int32 side enum: 1 left, 2 right node ranges are wrist 0 , thumb 1–4 , index 5–9 , middle 10–14 , ring 15–19 , and little finger 20–24 . each non-thumb finger runs from metacarpal through knuckle and two intermediate joints to the tip. treat publish_time as the opaque manustimestamp , not unix time. use recv_ns for timing intervals within one process run.
retargetingkit/axis-studio: axis studio axis studio sources stream noitom body motion from axis studio in calc broadcast mode. axisstudiosource converts the incoming avatar to a canonical z-up bodyframe for g1 retargeting. connect axis studio the bundled sdk runtime supports linux x86-64. from the retargetingkit repository: shell uv sync --extra axis --extra vis in axis studio, enable calc data broadcasting , set the destination to the retargetingkit workstation, and use udp port 7012 . if a firewall is active: shell sudo ufw allow 7012/udp preview g1 shell cuda_visible_devices=<free_gpu> uv run --extra axis --extra vis \ scripts/teleop/humanoid.py axisstudio_g1_sonic_viser \ --source.port 7012 --source.human-height 1.75 set --source.human-height to the user's height in meters. open http://localhost:8080 and check that g1 follows the streamed body motion. change --source.port if axis studio uses a different port. this rig also publishes commands to sonic. use axisstudio_g1_sonic to publish without viser. see humanoid teleoperation for simulation and g1 deployment.
retargetingkit/realsense: realsense realsense sources capture aligned rgb-d frames with realsense . the driver runs in a background process and exposes bgr color, raw depth, and camera intrinsics. l515 is the tested model; this camera driver is separate from the canonical teleoperation sources. check the camera from the retargetingkit repository: shell uv sync --extra realsense uv run --extra realsense python scripts/sources/realsense/print_intrinsics.py uv run --extra realsense --with opencv-python \ python scripts/sources/realsense/stream_rgbd.py the intrinsics script prints image resolution, focal lengths, principal point, and depth scale. the viewer shows color beside a depth visualization; press escape to close it. the driver uses the first connected camera by default. run rs-enumerate-devices to find a serial number, then pass --serial-number <serial> to either script. the realsense extra pins pyrealsense2<2.55 for l515 depth-stream compatibility. read frames in python python from retargetingkit.sources.cameras.realsense import realsense, realsenseconfig camera = realsense(realsenseconfig()) camera.start() color = camera.get_color() # (h, w, 3), uint8 bgr depth = camera.get_depth() # (h, w), uint16 sensor units intrinsics = camera.get_intrinsics() depth_meters = depth * intrinsics[6] camera.stop() intrinsics is [fx, fy, ppx, ppy, height, width, depth_scale] . frames align to the color stream by default; set realsenseconfig(align_to="depth") to align to depth. start() waits for the first captured frames.
retargetingkit/zed: zed zed sources capture bgr color and metric depth with a stereolabs zed camera. zed runs capture in a background process and exposes frames and intrinsics. it is a standalone camera driver and requires a cuda-capable nvidia gpu. install the sdk install the zed sdk for the workstation's ubuntu and cuda versions. stereolabs publishes one python binding wheel per python version (3.10–3.14) for zed sdk 5.2, linux x86-64 ; select the one matching the project's interpreter: shell py=$(uv run python -c 'import sys; print(f"cp{sys.version_info.major}{sys.version_info.minor}")') pyzed="https://download.stereolabs.com/zedsdk/5.2/whl/linux_x86_64/pyzed-5.2-$py-$py-linux_x86_64.whl" check the camera shell uv run --with "$pyzed" --with opencv-python \ python scripts/sources/zed/stream_rgbd.py the viewer shows color beside a depth visualization; press escape to close it. it defaults to hd1080 , 30 fps, and ultra depth mode. set --serial-number <serial> to select a camera, or use --resolution , --fps , and --depth-mode to change capture settings. read frames in python python from retargetingkit.sources.cameras.zed import zed, zedconfig camera = zed(zedconfig(resolution="hd1080", depth_mode="ultra")) camera.start() color = camera.get_color() # (h, w, 3), uint8 bgr depth = camera.get_depth() # (h, w), float32 meters intrinsics = camera.get_intrinsics() camera.stop() intrinsics is [fx, fy, cx, cy, height, width] for the left camera. depth is already in meters and needs no scale conversion.
retargetingkit/xarm: xarm6 and xarm7 xarm6 and xarm7 targets control a six- or seven-joint xarm through the ufactory sdk. both drivers accept joint positions in radians and provide end-effector ik and teaching modes. connect find the controller ip on the power box and open http://<xarm_ip>:18333 for ufactory studio. from the retargetingkit checkout, install the driver: shell uv sync --extra xarm for xarm7, read five samples without enabling motion or sending position commands: shell uv run --extra xarm scripts/targets/xarm7/read_qpos.py \ --ip <xarm_ip> --samples 5 the xarm6 read_qpos.py script starts the active velocity controller, including motion enable and error clearing. treat it as a controller session. preview teleoperation with vision pro configured: shell uv run --extra vision-pro --extra vis scripts/teleop/arm.py \ visionpro_xarm7 --mode viser --source.ip <vision_pro_ip> use visionpro_xarm6 for xarm6. the preview does not connect the arm. the vision pro guide covers ip overrides and arm-hand rigs; quest 3 provides a separate controller workflow. use the driver this snippet starts a hardware controller and holds the measured pose. replace target_qpos with your desired joint vector to move the arm. python from retargetingkit.targets.arms.xarm7 import xarm7config, xarmmode arm = xarm7config("<xarm_ip>", mode=xarmmode.velocity).build() target_qpos = arm.get_qpos() # (7,), urdf radians arm.set_qpos(target_qpos) arm.close() for six joints, import xarm6config from retargetingkit.targets.arms.xarm6 . mode behavior velocity default; smooths position tracking through velocity control servo streams joint position targets teaching enables gravity-compensated teaching both drivers run a background control loop at 250 hz by default. starting a driver enables motion, clears warnings and errors, and selects the configured control mode.
retargetingkit/xhand: xhand xhand targets control 12 xhand joints through rs485 or ethercat. the driver accepts urdf radians and sends commands through a background loop at approximately 83 hz. connect install the xhand_controller wheel from the xhand vendor. there is no xhand package extra. for rs485, connect the adapter and confirm its serial port. the default baud rate is 3,000,000. read five state samples without starting the servo controller: shell uv run scripts/targets/xhand/read_qpos.py \ --serial-port /dev/ttyusb0 --samples 5 the output includes joint names, positions in radians, and shape checks. preview retargeting with a configured manus glove : shell uv run --extra manus --extra vis scripts/teleop/hand.py \ manus_xhand --mode viser after checking the preview, --mode both --target.serial-port /dev/ttyusb0 connects and commands the hand. the vision pro guide also covers visionpro_xhand and xarm7–xhand rigs. use the driver this starts the physical hand's servo process and holds its measured pose: python from retargetingkit.targets.hands.xhand import xhandconfig hand = xhandconfig(serial_port="/dev/ttyusb0").build() target_qpos = hand.get_qpos() # (12,), urdf radians hand.set_qpos(target_qpos) hand.close() use protocol="ethercat" in the config for ethercat. commands must contain 12 finite values in the driver's documented urdf order. check a small motion the following moves joint 4 by 0.05 radians and returns it to its starting position: shell uv run scripts/targets/xhand/open_close.py \ --serial-port /dev/ttyusb0 --joint 4 --delta 0.05 --reps 1 despite its filename, this diagnostic nudges one joint; it does not open and close all fingers.
retargetingkit/sharpa-hand: sharpa wave sharpa wave targets control 22 finger joints and read tactile measurements from five fingers per hand. the driver accepts joint positions in urdf radians and exposes position, velocity, and torque feedback. connect get the sharpa sdk from sharpa and extract it so ~/.retargetingkit/sharpa-sdk/ holds its lib/ and python/ folders. the sdk's native extension must match your python environment. if the native loader reports a missing libpython , add your python environment's library directory and ~/.retargetingkit/sharpa-sdk/lib to ld_library_path before launching. device_sn=none selects the first discovered hand. set a device serial number when several hands are connected. read five samples in floating mode: shell uv run scripts/targets/sharpa_hand/read_qpos.py --samples 5 this changes the hand to floating mode for backdriving and prints angles in degrees. the python api returns radians. preview retargeting with manus configured, preview optimization: shell uv run --extra manus --extra vis scripts/teleop/hand.py \ manus_sharpa --mode viser use manus_sharpa_neural for the curated neural model. --mode real or --mode both commands the physical hand; add --target.device-sn <serial> to select it. vision pro also supports hand-only and xarm–sharpa rigs. use the driver construction connects the hand, selects position mode, and starts sdk control: python from retargetingkit.targets.hands.sharpa_hand import sharpahand hand = sharpahand(speed_coeff=0.3, current_coeff=0.3) qpos, qvel, torque = hand.get_state() # each has 22 values hand.set_qpos(qpos) hand.close() use set_control_mode("floating") for backdriving and set_control_mode("position") to resume position control. read touch data fetch five samples from the right thumb: shell uv run scripts/targets/sharpa_hand/tactile_fetch.py \ --channel 0 --samples 5 --calibrate this connects the sdk in position mode and calibrates before reading. frames may contain raw , deform , and f6 data. the driver api uses channels 0–4 for right thumb through pinky and 5–9 for the left; the current diagnostic labels right-hand channels only. scripts/targets/sharpa_hand/wave_example.py --cycles 3 moves joint 7 by 3 degrees and returns it, three times.
retargetingkit/ability-hand: ability hand ability hand targets control the psyonic ability hand's six joints through a usb serial adapter. the driver accepts radians and runs a background servo process, with position commands ramped at 60 degrees per second by default. connect power and connect the hand according to its hardware manual. use a stable linux device path when available: shell ls /dev/serial/by-id/ uv sync --extra ability your user needs access to the serial device, commonly through the dialout group. the driver uses 460800 baud. preview teleoperation the named vision pro rig combines ability hand with xarm7: shell uv run --extra vision-pro --extra vis scripts/teleop/arm_hand.py \ visionpro_xarm7_ability --mode viser --source.ip <vision_pro_ip> this previews motion without opening either robot target. follow the vision pro guide to configure the arm ip and hand port before selecting real or both . use the driver starting the driver sends serial position commands, including zero-position commands during initial synchronization. the following is a hardware controller session: python from retargetingkit.targets.hands.ability_hand import abilityhandconfig hand = abilityhandconfig("/dev/serial/by-id/<ability_hand>").build() target_qpos = hand.get_qpos() # (6,), radians hand.set_qpos(target_qpos) hand.close() replace target_qpos with the desired hand pose for your control loop. check motion the diagnostic below opens and closes the physical hand once: shell uv run --extra ability scripts/targets/ability_hand/open_close.py \ --port /dev/serial/by-id/<ability_hand> --reps 1 scripts/targets/ability_hand/read_qpos.py also starts the active servo process and sends startup commands. it is not a passive serial reader.
retargetingkit/inspire: inspire hand inspire hand targets control six actuated finger joints over usb serial. the driver converts urdf radians to inspire's serial joint order and normalized position range. connect connect the serial adapter and give your user access to its device port. on linux this commonly requires membership in dialout ; log out and back in after changing groups. shell uv sync --extra inspire the combined g1 preset uses /dev/ttyusb0 for the left hand and /dev/ttyusb1 for the right, both at 115200 baud with hand id 1 . confirm the actual ports before connecting. use the driver python from retargetingkit.targets.hands.inspire import inspirehandconfig hand = inspirehandconfig("/dev/ttyusb0", 1, 115200).build() qpos = hand.get_qpos() # (6,), urdf radians hand.close() construction opens the serial connection and starts a background reader. commands begin after the first hand.set_qpos(target_qpos) call; feedback updates asynchronously. joint order is thumb rotation, thumb bend, index, middle, ring, and little finger. use hand.joint_names when aligning a robot model. teleoperate with pico after completing pico setup , run: shell uv run --extra pico --extra inspire scripts/teleop/humanoid_hand.py \ pico_g1_inspire --source.no-use-ankle-as-foot-target \ --left-hand.serial-port /dev/ttyusb0 \ --right-hand.serial-port /dev/ttyusb1 this connects both physical hands and publishes body motion to sonic. b toggles the right hand open/closed; y toggles the left. the rig has no preview mode and uses preset hand poses rather than tracked fingers. for continuous vision pro arm-hand control, use the visionpro_xarm7_inspire rig described in vision pro . for g1 deployment, follow humanoid teleoperation .
retargetingkit/g1: g1 and sonic g1 and sonic targets send retargeted g1 motion to gr00t whole-body control through a sonic zmq publisher. the deployment stack executes the policy in mujoco or on a real g1. prepare the deployment stack install and configure gr00t-wholebodycontrol on the deployment machine. for the bundled simulation launcher, place the checkout at: text thirdparty/gr00t-wholebodycontrol/ the launcher expects its .venv_sim environment and gear_sonic_deploy/deploy.sh to be ready, and requires tmux . robot descriptions and collision assets come from robokit. start a recorded stream from the retargetingkit checkout: shell uv run --extra vis scripts/teleop/humanoid.py bvh_g1_sonic_viser this publishes a sample bvh clip on port 5556 and opens viser. _viser adds a viewer while keeping the sonic stream active. for a viewer without a publisher, use the first example in humanoid teleoperation . in a second terminal, launch simulation: shell bash scripts/tools/launch_sonic_sim.sh in the deployment pane, press ] , then enter , to start the policy. the script creates a sonic_sim tmux session and replaces an existing session with that name. connect a real g1 after validating the retargeted motion and preparing the robot deployment stack, run this from its gear_sonic_deploy directory on the robot: shell bash deploy.sh real --input-type zmq \ --zmq-host <workstation_ip> --zmq-port 5556 --zmq-topic pose this selects real robot deployment. use the deployment controls and physical emergency stop described by your g1 setup. the workstation must run a sonic preset and be reachable on port 5556 . what the stream contains sonictarget receives a baseposeqposcommand , estimates and smooths joint velocities, and converts 29 joint positions and velocities from g1 urdf order to sonic order. it sends the root quaternion and joint data on topic pose ; root translation is omitted. the default publisher binds tcp://*:5556 . live axis studio, pico, and dual inspire hand workflows are covered in humanoid teleoperation .
retargetingkit/rby1: rby1-a rby1-a targets control the rby1-a's seven-joint right arm through the rainbow robotics sdk, with separate commands for the two-joint head. this is a standalone driver; no named teleoperation rig is currently registered. connect find the robot's grpc address in its control panel, then install: shell uv sync --extra rby1 use the complete address, including the port, such as <rby1_ip>:50051 . use the driver building the driver powers on the robot, enables servos and the control manager, and starts a command stream. this snippet holds the measured right-arm pose: python from retargetingkit.targets.humanoids.rby1 import rby1aconfig, rby1amode arm = rby1aconfig("<rby1_ip>:50051", mode=rby1amode.velocity).build() target_qpos = arm.get_qpos() # (7,), radians arm.set_qpos(target_qpos) arm.close() replace target_qpos with the desired right-arm joint positions. get_head_qpos() and set_head_qpos() expose the head separately. close the driver with close() . mode behavior velocity default; converts position error to a smoothed command servo streams position targets with a velocity limit teaching enables right-arm gravity compensation the background loop runs at 100 hz by default. head position commands remain active in all three modes. inspect feedback shell uv run --extra rby1 scripts/targets/rby1/read_qpos.py \ --ip <rby1_ip>:50051 this script starts the same active controller, including power and servo enable. it prints feedback while holding the initial pose; it is not a passive state reader.
retargetingkit/dexmate: dexmate vega-1 dexmate vega-1 targets control vega-1's torso, head, and both arms through the dexmate sdk. the driver exposes 20 joints and is available as a standalone target; no named teleoperation rig is currently registered. connect configure robot discovery and zenoh communication for your dexmate setup, then install: shell uv sync --extra dexmate retargetingkit pins dexcontrol==0.4.4 and dexcomm==0.4.2 for the supported discovery stack. read current joint positions without sending a motion target: shell uv run --extra dexmate scripts/targets/dexmate/read_qpos.py press ctrl+c to close the connection. use the driver python from retargetingkit.targets.humanoids.dexmate import dexmateconfig robot = dexmateconfig().build() qpos = robot.get_qpos() # (20,), radians print(dict(zip(robot.joint_names, qpos))) robot.close() use robot.joint_names to align commands with the model: group joints torso torso_j1 through torso_j3 head head_j1 through head_j3 left arm l_arm_j1 through l_arm_j7 right arm r_arm_j1 through r_arm_j7 this is also the order of get_qpos() and set_qpos() . send motion with an open connection and a desired 20-joint target_qpos , choose one command style: python robot.set_qpos(target_qpos) # publish repeatedly in your control loop the default wait_time=0 publishes a setpoint and returns immediately. for one interpolated move that blocks until completion: python robot.set_qpos(target_qpos, wait_time=3.0, max_vel=0.2) max_vel is in radians per second. both forms command the physical robot; call robot.close() when finished.

graspkit/overview: overview overview graspkit is an end-to-end toolkit for manipulation across various robot embodiments, including grippers and dexterous hands. it synthesizes grasps, plans trajectories, trains policies, and deploys them in simulation or on real robots; it is built on top of robokit . real-world grasping with dexterous robot hands in san diego. key features fast grasp optimization. gpu optimizers refine thousands of grasp seeds per batch against cached scene geometry. see grasp optimization . performant policy training. train grasp policies on processed point clouds and successful trajectories, with multi-gpu support. see training . across embodiments. use grippers and dexterous hands in arm, hand, and humanoid configurations. see the robot catalog . simulation validation. filter and motion-plan grasps, then test them in physics simulation. see simulation deployment . real-world validation. run trained policies on xarm and vega robots with calibrated cameras and collision-checked motions. see real deployment . fast grasp optimization performant policy training all arms, all hands real-world robustness how it works stage role read more scene descriptions objects, scales and poses on a table, as msgpack. scene descriptions grasp optimization energy minimization to grasp poses, then filters, motion planning and sim validation. grasp optimization rendering point-cloud observations of the same scenes, from calibrated cameras. pipeline training a cvae policy that maps an object point cloud to pre-grasp, grasp and post-grasp poses. training deployment policy inference plus trajectory building, in sim or on hardware. sim , real for the graph of stages and the artifacts between them, see core overview . quick links quickstart installation github website
graspkit/quickstart: quickstart quickstart try it without installing run this to start the interactive grasp gallery: shell uvx --from graspkit python -m graspkit.gallery.grasp_optim pick a hand, arm, and object. press optimize to generate grasps, then browse them with the grasp slider. the gallery caches results for the next visit. optimize one grasp after installing , run the smallest grasp optimization example: shell uv run src/graspkit/examples/grasp_optim/01_basic.py it optimizes xhand grasps for one ycb object and opens a viser page to browse the results. grasp optimization needs a cuda gpu. more examples the scripts below are runnable. paths are relative to the repository root. directory scripts src/graspkit/examples/grasp_optim 01_basic.py , 02_table.py , 03_arm.py , 04_sim_valid.py , 05_table_sim_valid.py , 06_arm_sim_valid.py , 07_mj_sim_valid.py scripts/launch.py run an experiment from grasp optimization through policy training. see the full pipeline . example usage: shell uv run src/graspkit/examples/grasp_optim/02_table.py
