graspkit/grasp-optim:
grasp optimization grasp optimization (grasp_optim) a floating hand optimizing a grasp. an arm and hand optimized together on a fixed base. graspkit.stages.grasp_optim synthesizes grasps on a floating or fixed base. it optimizes them on the gpu (warp) with a gradient-descent or levenberg-marquardt backend, then plans grasp trajectories and keeps only the grasps that pass simulation validation. this tutorial covers the main grasp optimization workflows. the logic lives in [src/graspkit/stages/grasp_optim](../../src/graspkit/stages/grasp_optim/) ; runnable clis for optimization, validation, and visualization are in [scripts/stages/grasp_optim](../../scripts/stages/grasp_optim/) . how grasp optimization works sample initial hand poses around the target object. run the grasp optimizer ( warp_gd or warp_lm backend) to get 3-frame grasps (pre-grasp, grasp, post-grasp), with a floating or fixed base. if filters are enabled (hand-axis cone, contact-avoid, penetration), mark the grasps that fail them. filters run first inside the traj builder. the traj builder motion-plans the 3 frames into grasp trajectories. simulation validation keeps the grasps that pass filters, planning and sim. flowchart td input[input

scene description
robot config] subgraph optim[grasp optimization] direction tb sample[1. sampler
→ initial hand poses] opt["2. graspoptimizer (warp_gd / warp_lm)
→ 3-frame grasps"] filter["3. filters (optional)"] plan["4. trajbuilder
→ grasp traj"] sim["5. simulation validation"] sample --> opt --> filter --> plan --> sim end output[return grasps] input --> sample sim --> output quick start prerequisites: uv sync --extra maniskill --extra spconv , a cuda gpu. assets (scenes, object meshes, robot urdfs) download automatically on first use. run grasp optimization for a registered experiment config (here xhand on the dex1b v0.5 tabletop mini set) with scripts/launch.py . shell uv run scripts/launch.py xhand_right_dex1b_v0_5_mini_tabletop \ --steps optimize_grasps \ --grasp_optim.max_scenes 32 \ --grasp_output_dir data/optim_data/xhand_grasps/quickstart --grasp_optim.max_scenes 32 keeps it to about two minutes on one gpu; drop it to run all 5500 scenes. the sections below build the same stage step by step in python. sampling initial poses init samples drawn with the palm-down cone below: red is the hand axis ( palm_forward ), gray is the target (world -z). both start at the wrist; the label is their angle, always within the 60 deg cone. optimize() starts from the optimizer's sampler; call it directly to inspect the initial poses: python from dataclasses import replace import torch from graspkit.configs.robot.xhand import xhand_right from graspkit.gallery.grasp_optim import gallery_scene from graspkit.stages.grasp_optim import graspoptimconfig, scenegeom, warpgraspoptimizer scene = gallery_scene("ycb/mustard_bottle") # scenedescription: the bottle on a table whose top is z=0 device = torch.device("cuda:0") # customize the approach config = graspoptimconfig( distance_lower=0.05, # wrist 5-15 cm from the closest object point distance_upper=0.15, hand_axis="palm_forward", # hand_coord_spec axis to constrain hand_axis_target=(0.0, 0.0, -1.0), # toward world -z filter_hand_axis_max_angle_deg=60.0, # cone half-angle ) optimizer = warpgraspoptimizer(config, xhand_right, device) init_qpos = optimizer.sampler.sample(scenegeom([scene], device=device), num_samples_per_scene=8) grasp optimization optimize() samples init poses with the same sampler, then minimizes the grasp energy on the gpu. reusing scene and the palm-down config from above: python config = replace(config, optimizer_backend="warp_gd") # or "warp_lm" (levenberg-marquardt) optimizer = warpgraspoptimizer(config, xhand_right, device) grasp_qpos = optimizer.optimize([scene], num_samples_per_scene=8) # (1, 8, 18) filtering grasps grasp filters live in grasptrajbuilderconfig and run first inside grasptrajbuilder.build() . they only mark grasps, they don't drop them. call filter_grasps to run them alone, without motion planning: python from graspkit.configs.experiment_config import grasptrajbuilderconfig from graspkit.datasets.graspkit_data import graspkitdata from graspkit.stages.grasp_traj_build import grasptrajbuilder traj_builder = grasptrajbuilder( grasptrajbuilderconfig( floating_base_robot_config=xhand_right, contact_avoid_filter=true, # contact links closer to the object than their paired avoid links pen_filter=true, # hand spheres overlap the object by at most pen_filter_threshold pen_filter_threshold=0.005, hand_axis="palm_forward", # palm normal within 60 deg of world -z (top-down grasps) hand_axis_target=(0.0, 0.0, -1.0), filter_hand_axis_max_angle_deg=60.0, ), device, ) batch = graspkitdata(scene_ids=[scene.scene_id], scene_descriptions=[scene], grasp_qpos=grasp_qpos) success, metrics = traj_builder.filter_grasps(batch, torch.ones(grasp_qpos.shape[:2], dtype=torch.bool, device=device)) kept = grasp_qpos[success] # (n_kept, dofs) building grasp trajectories build() runs the filters above, then motion-plans a pre-grasp -> grasp -> lift trajectory for every grasp. rejected grasps are still planned; drop them with filter_success : python traj_builder = grasptrajbuilder( grasptrajbuilderconfig(floating_base_robot_config=xhand_right, contact_avoid_filter=true), device ) batch = graspkitdata(scene_ids=[scene.scene_id], scene_descriptions=[scene], grasp_qpos=grasp_qpos) batch, filter_success = traj_builder.build(batch) simulation validation the sim evaluator rolls out each planned trajectory in maniskill, pokes the object with external forces, and reports which grasps still lift it: python from graspkit.configs.env_config import msenvconfig from graspkit.configs.experiment_config import envconfig from graspkit.envs import build_env evaluator = build_env( envconfig( ms_env_config=msenvconfig(robot_uid="xhand_right_floating_base"), load_scenes=true, control_freq=50, object_mass=1.0, target_lift_dist=0.08, num_envs=8, num_perturbations=4, perturbation_magnitude=5.0, perturbation_step_range=(-25, -5), ), xhand_right, device, ) eval_success = evaluator.evaluate(batch)["success"].to(device) # (1, 8) bool kept = grasp_qpos[filter_success & eval_success] # (n_kept, dofs) evaluator.close() outputs one {scene_id}.h5 per scene with grasp_qpos , pre_grasp_qpos , post_grasp_qpos of shape (n, d) : d = hand joints (fixed base) or xyz + euler rxyz + hand joints (floating). .optim_complete marks the stage done. see data_format.md . code map code role src/graspkit/stages/grasp_optim/sampler.py init pose sampler src/graspkit/stages/grasp_optim/warp_optimizer.py warpgraspoptimizer src/graspkit/stages/grasp_filters.py grasp filters ( ori , pen , contactavoid ) src/graspkit/stages/grasp_traj_build/builder.py grasptrajbuilder : filters + motion planning src/graspkit/envs/ build_env sim evaluator scripts/launch.py runs an experiment config end to end

a later launch skips the stage while that marker exists. minimal training loop the experiment config holds the three pieces: dataset ( datasetconfig ), agent ( grasppolicyconfig ), and trainer ( trainerconfig ). python import torch from torch.utils.data import dataloader from graspkit.configs.experiment import build_experiment_config from graspkit.datasets.grasp_dataset import graspdataset from graspkit.models.grasp_policy import build_grasp_policy cfg = build_experiment_config("xhand_right_dex1b_v0_5_mini_tabletop") dataset = graspdataset(cfg.dataset, cfg.processed_data_path, cfg.scene_description_path, split="train") loader = dataloader(dataset, batch_size=cfg.trainer.batch_size, shuffle=true, num_workers=4, drop_last=true) policy = build_grasp_policy(cfg.agent, cfg.robot_config, "cuda") optimizer = torch.optim.adamw(policy.parameters(), lr=cfg.trainer.lr) for batch in loader: obs = {k: v.cuda() for k, v in batch["observations"].items()} loss = policy(obs, batch["actions"].cuda())["loss"] optimizer.zero_grad() loss.backward() optimizer.step() policy.eval() with torch.no_grad(): grasps = policy.get_action(obs, num_samples_per_scene=8) # (b, 8, 3, d): pre / grasp / post the real trainer ( src/graspkit/stages/trainer.py ) adds lr scheduling, ddp, checkpoints, tensorboard, and simulation evaluation through trainer.evaluator . evaluate a checkpoint evaluation samples one trajectory per scene, runs grasp filtering and motion planning, then rolls the trajectory out in the configured simulator: shell uv run scripts/stages/train/train.py xhand_right_dex1b_v0_5_mini_tabletop \ --trainer.eval_only \ --ckpt_path logs/train/xhand_right_dex1b_v0_5_mini_tabletop/checkpoints/best_eval_success_rate.pt the command reports simulation success, penetration pass rate, and their joint rate. per-scene results are saved to logs/eval/.json .
graspkit/pipeline:
pipeline the full pipeline (launch.py) scripts/launch.py turns a set of scene descriptions into a trained grasp policy. one experiment name selects an experimentconfig whose steps run in order: render point-cloud observations, synthesize and validate grasps, join both into a training dataset, and train an open-loop policy. this tutorial explains what each stage does and how data flows between them. for stage deep-dives see the grasp_optim tutorial and the training tutorial ; for every parameter see the config reference . overview the default steps are ("render_data", "optimize_grasps", "process_sim_data", "train") . observations and actions are produced independently from the same scene descriptions, then joined per scene. robot_config decides what the optimizer outputs: a floating hand yields floating grasps, an arm+hand robot yields fixed-base grasps. the grasptrajbuilder filters them, optionally ik-converts floating grasps onto the fixed robot ( convert_to_fixed=true ), and plans the grasp trajectory; the evaluator keeps only grasps that survive a sim rollout. every stage writes a completion marker next to its output ( .render_complete , .optim_complete , ...). a later launch skips any stage whose marker exists, so an interrupted pipeline resumes where it stopped. quick start prerequisites: uv sync --extra maniskill --extra spconv , cuda gpus. assets (scenes, object meshes, robot urdfs) download automatically on first use. experiments live in src/graspkit/configs/experiment/ and are registered by name in its __init__.py . shell # full pipeline on 4 gpus uv run scripts/launch.py xhand_right_dex1b_v0_5_mini_tabletop --gpus 0,1,2,3 # run a subset of steps; any nested config field is a cli flag through tyro uv run scripts/launch.py xhand_right_dex1b_v0_5_mini_tabletop --steps optimize_grasps \ --grasp_optim.num_attempts 2 # rerun from a step: deletes that step's marker + output and everything downstream uv run scripts/launch.py xhand_right_dex1b_v0_5_mini_tabletop --restart-from process_sim_data # append mode: keep the restart step's output, delete only its marker (top up grasps) uv run scripts/launch.py xhand_right_dex1b_v0_5_mini_tabletop \ --restart-from optimize_grasps --append renderer -> point-cloud observations renders every scene through the calibrated real camera so training observations match deployment. flowchart td sd[(scene descriptions)] calib[(camera calibration
extrinsic + intrinsic .json)] cam[per-scene camera poses

graspkit/sim-deploy: sim deployment sim deployment three ways to run a trained policy in simulation: inside training, as a reproducible benchmark, or interactively in the deploy ui. during training set trainerconfig.evaluator to an envconfig and the trainer evaluates every eval_freq iterations on rank 0: it samples actions, builds trajectories with grasptrajbuilder , rolls them out, and reports a success rate plus a report-only penetration pass rate ( penetration <= eval_pen_threshold , 5 mm by default). shell # evaluate an existing checkpoint, no training uv run scripts/stages/train/train.py <experiment> --trainer.eval-only --ckpt-path <ckpt> results land in logs/train/<experiment>/eval_success.jsonl , tensorboard ( eval/success_rate , eval/pen_pass_rate ) and checkpoints/best_eval_success_rate.pt . eval-only runs also write per-scene results to logs/eval/<experiment>.json . knobs on envconfig : num_envs (2048), num_seeds (a grasp must survive every seed), enable_perturbation with perturbation_magnitude / perturbation_step_range / num_perturbations , the task ( control_freq , object_mass , target_lift_dist , ...), and mj_env_config / isaac_env_config to pick a backend other than maniskill. trainerconfig adds eval_num_envs , max_eval_batches and eval_pen_threshold . maniskill counts a tabletop grasp as a success when the hand is strictly grasping and the object has risen by target_lift_dist ; with floating_object it is grasp-only. as a benchmark the default checkpoint mode of scripts/benchmark/grasp_policy/evaluate_policy.py makes every prediction before any physics, asserts the eval scenes are disjoint from the training and validation ids, and records actions, trajectories, and per-scene results. shell pythonhashseed=0 cuda_visible_devices=<free gpu> uv run scripts/benchmark/grasp_policy/evaluate_policy.py \ --checkpoint <ckpt> --output <report.json> \ --evaluation-experiment <experiment> --observations-path <processed.h5> \ --require-native --require-object-disjoint the checkpoint must carry experiment , policy_config , agent and training keys; plain trainer checkpoints hold only agent , so use the packaging scripts under scripts/stages/train/ . the report gives raw (sim success), penetration (deepest hand-sphere overlap into the object at the grasp pose, in metres) and joint = raw & penetration <= 0.005 . that 5 mm threshold is fixed in the script, independent of eval_pen_threshold . the same runner supports tabletop observations with --mode pc_open_loop , pc_closed_loop , or rgb_closed_loop . choose --robot from arx_x5 , panda_allegro , or agilex_aloha , and --arm-mode from floating_ik or arm_aware . each scene gets one selected grasp execution; tabletop results are written to a .jsonl output. interactively shell uv run --extra sam2 scripts/deploy/deploy.py --env sim \ --exp-config-name <experiment> --ckpt-path <ckpt> the sim path runs one environment, takes scenes from the experiment's msgpack split, and drives the same staged viser ui the real robot uses — capture, segment, check grasp, deploy. --auto (sim only) takes the segmentation prompt from the simulator's ground-truth mask and prints the sam2-vs-gt mask iou; --scene-id and --num-scenes choose scenes, --deploy-batch-size replays several grasps at once. mujoco instead of maniskill setting envconfig.mj_env_config selects mujoco, which is the only backend for hands with no maniskill agent ( shadow_right_mj , xarm7_xhand_right_mj , vega_sharpa_*_mj ). it runs on cpu in a spawned pool of up to 48 workers and evaluates a grasp pose rather than a trajectory: setting="fc" — free-space force closure: grip, then hold against six axis-aligned forces; fails if the object translates past trans_thre or rotates past angle_thre . setting="tabletop" — grip, apply a downward wrench (gravity is disabled), lift 20 cm, and require slip below lift_slip_thre , rotation below angle_thre , and contact after the lift. use timestep=0.001 for actuated arm+hand models; the 0.004 default flings the object. pitfalls msenv warns when num_envs and the sample count are not multiples of each other: the mismatch forces a reconfiguration per batch, which dominates the runtime. evaluating far fewer grasps than num_envs is wasteful; the env warns about that too. reconfiguration only happens when the batch's scene set changes, so sort work by scene. seeding is explicit: evaluate_policy.py asserts pythonhashseed=0 ; seed_everything does not enable deterministic kernels unless asked.
graspkit/real-deploy: real deployment real deployment running a trained policy on hardware: capture a point cloud, predict a grasp, build a trajectory, execute it, release, and park. these scripts move a real robot. run them yourself, with the e-stop in reach — never from an automated agent. prerequisites the rig's xarm extra, plus sam2 for segmentation. a checkpoint whose robot matches the rig: deploy asserts that the actuated joint names of the policy's robot and the hardware robot are identical. hardware presets configs/real_env.py holds one realenvconfig per rig; --real-env-config-name selects it, and an experiment can name a default through real_env_config_name . preset arm hand camera xarm7_xhand_right xarm7 xhand realsense xarm6_sharpa_right xarm6 sharpa realsense xarm7_ability_right xarm7 ability (channel reindex) realsense each preset also carries the planning table ( table_size , table_xy , table_z ), the point-cloud crop centre ( workspace_center ), the streaming rate ( control_hz ) and how many depth frames to median-combine. experiments need --real-env-config-name , a fixed-base trajectory and camera_frame="robot" . run it shell uv run --extra sam2 --extra xarm scripts/deploy/deploy.py --env real \ --exp-config-name xhand_right_dex1b_v0_5_mini_tabletop_fixed_eval \ --ckpt-path <checkpoint> --real-env-config-name xarm7_xhand_right every stage waits for a button in the viser page: capture — reset to the init pose, grab rgb (median of depth_frames depth frames). segment — click the object; sam 2 turns the clicks into a mask, which becomes the cropped, subsampled point cloud in the robot base frame. check grasp — the policy samples --num-samples grasps; the trajectory builder converts and plans them, and the top eight valid candidates are shown. for a floating-base policy the cloud is mean-centred and the centroid added back; --pc-offset nudges it. --post-grasp-hand-close-scale rescales the closing motion. deploy — the trajectory is streamed phase by phase at the rig's control_hz . the deploy until step slider stops mid-trajectory so you can compare commanded and measured joint positions against the live cloud, then resume. release and park — the hand opens in place, then a collision-checked plan returns the arm to the init pose against a table raised by 5 cm. there is no reset afterwards. --loop keeps cycling; without it, a capture with no valid grasp is an error. calibration the deploy path reads a base-frame camera extrinsic and a camera intrinsic from the shipped calibration files ( assets/calib.py , wired into the experiment's renderer.camera_poses_path and camera_intrinsic_path ). inspect the result with uv run scripts/tools/visualize_camera_extrinsic.py --experiment-name ... (offline) or uv run --extra xarm scripts/deploy/visualize_calib.py (live). the park plan raises the table by 5 cm because the optimizer otherwise rides the collision margin.
graspkit/concepts-overview: core overview core overview how the stages fit together, what flows between them, and where robokit ends and graspkit begins. the graph text scene descriptions (msgpack) scripts/stages/scene_desc/* | +---------------------------+ | | [render_data] [optimize_grasps] (sharded: scenes[rank::world_size]) renderer / maniskill warpgraspoptimizer kinematic replay, -> grasptrajbuilder: filters -> (ik convert) -> motion plan point-cloud obs -> optional in-loop sim eval | | rendered_data_path grasp_output_dir (h5 per scene) (h5 per scene: pre / grasp / post qpos) +------------+--------------+ | [process_sim_data] -> processed_data_path (obs + actions per scene) | [train] graspdataset -> trainer (ddp through torchrun) | logs/train/<name>/checkpoints/*.pt scripts/launch.py dispatches these by name; the order is whatever experimentconfig.steps lists, by default render_data , optimize_grasps , process_sim_data , train . a fifth step, sample_point_cloud , exists for object-only clouds but no shipped experiment uses it. stages stage in out config optimize_grasps scene descriptions grasp h5 (pre/grasp/post qpos) graspoptimconfig , grasptrajbuilderconfig render_data scene descriptions rendered h5 (point clouds, segmentation, camera poses) rendererconfig process_sim_data rendered h5 + grasp h5 processed h5 (obs joined to actions) experimentconfig train processed h5 checkpoints trainerconfig , datasetconfig , grasppolicyconfig grasp optimization is the compound stage: it optimizes, then filters (hand-axis cone, contact-avoid, penetration, rest pose), optionally ik-converts floating grasps onto an arm, plans a trajectory, and keeps only what a physics evaluator accepts. resuming and sharding each stage writes a completion marker ( .optim_complete , .render_complete , .process_sim_data_complete , .train_complete ) and skips itself when the marker exists. with multiple ranks the marker is written per rank and promoted once every rank is done; s3:// outputs get no marker. --restart-from <step> deletes the marker and outputs for that step and everything downstream, --append keeps the output and deletes only the marker. grasp optimization additionally resumes per scene: it re-runs scenes whose output is smaller than min_grasps_threshold . only grasp optimization uses every gpu, one process per card with scenes striped across ranks; non-zero ranks sleep 20 s so rank 0 compiles the warp kernels first. rendering and processing pin to the first gpu, and training goes through torchrun . artifacts graspkitdata is the tensor payload that crosses stages, in a padded (b, k, ...) or packed (n, ...) layout, saved as hdf5. scene descriptions are msgpack with a train/test split. the processed file holds data/<scene>/obs , data/<scene>/actions and meta/action_{mean,std} ; the trainer consumes it through graspdataset . floating base versus fixed base robotconfig.base_type decides the action layout: a floating hand prepends six base dofs, baked as [xyz, euler_rxyz, hand joints] . a floating hand is always optimized with the floating-base sampler, and the levenberg-marquardt backend is floating-only. setting grasptrajbuilderconfig.convert_to_fixed filters those grasps and ik-converts them onto an arm before planning; inside grasp optimization the conversion is always off, so the planner plans for the robot being optimized. robokit versus graspkit robokit supplies the cost terms, optimizers, contact sampling, warp scenes, sdf baking, the robot model and the motion planner. graspkit owns the energy assembly, the init samplers, the grasp filters, the scene-description adapter, the renderer, the datasets, the policy and the trainer. code graduates to robokit only when a second consumer exists.
graspkit/grasp-optim-backends: grasp optimization backends grasp optimization algorithms: warp_gd and warp_lm how the two grasp-optimizer backends work and when to use which. for running the stage see the grasp_optim tutorial ; for every parameter see the grasp optimization api . the problem grasp synthesis is energy minimization over a batch of grasps. each grasp optimizes the robot configuration q : hand joints, plus arm joints (fixed base) or a free se(3) base pose (floating hand), and a discrete contact assignment: which num_contact_points of the robot's predefined contact candidates are active. the energy is a weighted sum of residual terms (robokit terms.dense.* ): term pulls toward distancetask active contact points on the object surface forceclosuretask contact normals that balance external wrenches (stability) scenecollisiontask hand collision spheres out of the scene (object + table) selfcollisiontask links out of each other positionlimit joints inside their limits fingertipdistancetask (optional) fingertip spheres onto the surface handupangletask (optional) hand-up axis at least angle_z_min from world +z both backends share this formulation, the init samplers, and the warp scene geometry (sdf volumes / mesh bvhs). the energy is highly non-convex and the contact assignment is discrete, so plain gradient descent gets stuck; each backend has its own escape mechanism. warp_gd: simulated-annealing gradient descent warpgraspoptimizer ( warp_optimizer.py , backend warp_gd ) runs each grasp as an independent annealing chain for num_iters (~10k) iterations, dexgraspnet-style. one iteration: rmsprop step on the continuous variables; step size decays over time, joints are clamped to limits. with probability switch_possibility , propose a re-drawn contact set. evaluate the proposal's energy and gradient. metropolis accept: lower energy always wins; worse by d is accepted with probability exp(-d / t) , where the temperature t cools over time. rejected grasps roll back. high t early lets grasps explore pose and contact assignment jointly; as t cools the chain settles into a low-energy basin. the whole iteration is captured as one cuda graph, so the long loop has almost no launch overhead. works for floating and fixed-base robots alike, which makes it the default backend. warp_lm: multi-seed levenberg-marquardt warpgraspoptimizer (backend warp_lm ) treats the same energy as nonlinear least squares and applies robokit's lmoptimizer : curvature-aware steps converge in tens of iterations instead of thousands. a single lm run is purely local, so exploration comes from: multi-seed : every init grasp spawns 24 jittered copies solved in parallel; the lowest-energy seed wins. contact resampling : lm cannot differentiate the discrete contacts, so every 8 iterations each candidate is joined by a copy with a fresh random contact set; both take the next lm steps, and the one with the lower energy stays. warp_lm supports floating bases only. to target an arm+hand robot, set enable_ik_scoring=true : inits are pre-filtered by arm-ik reachability against the fixed-base robot and final seeds are ranked by energy + reachability penalty , so the grasps grasptrajbuilder later ik-converts onto the arm are actually reachable. choosing a backend warp_gd warp_lm method rmsprop + simulated annealing multi-seed levenberg-marquardt exploration metropolis accept over pose + contacts 24 seeds + periodic contact resampling iterations ~10000 first-order steps 64 curvature-aware steps speed baseline typically 2-3x faster robots floating and fixed base floating base only ( enable_ik_scoring bridges to arms) rule of thumb: warp_gd for fixed-base robots or when maximum exploration matters; warp_lm for floating-hand throughput, with enable_ik_scoring if the grasps will be converted to an arm. both are compared in scripts/benchmark/grasp_opt/bench_grasp_optim.py .
graspkit/concepts-sim: simulation simulation graspkit uses two physics backends behind one interface: maniskill (gpu, batched, full rollouts) and mujoco (cpu, grasp-pose scoring). a third path, the renderer, uses the maniskill scene without stepping physics at all. one interface baseenv fixes the contract: reset , get_qpos , step_qpos , get_info , get_rgb , get_pointcloud , evaluate , close , with evaluate returning per-grasp success and, when asked, rollout records ( qpos , obj_pose , scene_id , success , grasp_index ). build_env picks the implementation: mjenv when envconfig.mj_env_config is set, otherwise msenv ; realenv is imported lazily so the sim path never needs the hardware extras. mjenv implements only evaluate — it scores grasps offline and raises on the interactive methods. realenv is the mirror image: it drives hardware but has no ground truth, so evaluate raises. maniskill the env is registered as dexgrasp . a scene description becomes actors grouped by mesh and scale, built in sorted order because physx contact outcomes depend on insertion order, with mass forced to object_mass and a merged target actor per scene. a table is added unless floating_object is set, which also disables gravity on the object. success is "strictly grasped and lifted past target_lift_dist ", or grasp-only for a floating object; grasping itself means at least two contact links pushing with more than half a newton. floating hands can be driven two ways: virtual joints — the agent's first six joints are pd-driven by the floating_base controller. this is the default for *_floating_base agent uids. static base — when the maniskill agent is hand-only but the pipeline robot is floating, the six base dofs are stripped from the qpos and applied as per-environment root poses instead. the base is pinned at the final grasp pose, which tests the grasp without an approach sweep or base pd shake. joint order differs between maniskill's observation order ( robot.active_joints ) and its action order ( controller.joints ); reindex_utils converts in both directions, and picking the wrong one silently scrambles a bimanual robot. agent uids follow the robot config name, with _floating_base appended for floating hands. the env lists the 21 supported uids. mujoco mjdexgraspenv builds a model with mjspec: the hand's mjcf, a table box that collides with the object but never the hand, and the object as convex pieces added in a fixed order because mujoco sums geom inertia in that order. gravity is disabled; a downward wrench stands in for it. density is rescaled so the object weighs obj_mass . two protocols: fc — force closure in free space: pregrasp, grasp, squeeze, then hold against six axis-aligned forces scaled by fc_force_scale ; failure is translation past trans_thre or rotation past angle_thre . tabletop — grip, apply the wrench, lift 20 cm (mocap root for floating hands, damped least-squares arm ik for fixed-base rigs), then require slip below lift_slip_thre , rotation below angle_thre , and live contact after the lift. both bail out immediately when the initial pose is already penetrating past max_pene . beyond success, the evaluator reports hand-object and self penetration, contact count, contact distance and consistency. a handspec adapts a hand: its mjcf path, whether it is mocap-driven, finger prefixes, the bodies that count as contact and fingertips, and — for fixed-base rigs — which body to lift and which joints the ik may move. mujoco is cpu-only and not thread-safe, so mjenv runs a spawned pool of up to 48 workers, one evaluator each. spawn, not fork: forking a cuda-initialized parent deadlocks. the renderer mani_skill/renderer.py ( build_renderer ) makes its own dexgrasp env with num_envs environments and a point-cloud observation mode, then never steps physics: it writes qpos and object poses, flushes the gpu kinematics, and reads observations. batching is over (scene, view) pairs. segmentation ids select what survives ( extract_segments wins over remove_segments ), and points are cropped either in the camera frame or in the world frame offset by each scene's table position. msenv.get_pointcloud replicates that crop exactly, so deployment clouds match the training distribution. choosing a backend maniskill mujoco hardware gpu, batched cpu, process pool scores full approach → grasp → lift rollouts, with perturbation forces a grasp pose: force closure or a lift gives success, observations, rgb and point clouds success plus penetration and contact metrics robots the 21 agents with maniskill uids any hand with an mjcf handspec hands with no maniskill agent (menagerie shadow, the _mj xarm+xhand and vega+sharpa rigs) can only be validated in mujoco, which is why several experiments use it as their in-loop grasp filter.
graspkit/concepts-policies: models and policies models and policies grasppolicy in src/graspkit/models/grasp_policy.py maps an observation to a grasp: three hand poses (pre-grasp, grasp, post-grasp) that the trajectory builder turns into an executable motion. open and closed loop use the same policy. the execution controller decides when to observe and predict again; the benchmark's closed-loop mode refreshes the observation and replans at step 75. the policy selects cvae from models/cvae.py or flowmatching from models/flow_matching.py using generative_model ( cvae , flow , flow_transformer ). both generators expose forward , decode and sample ; access the selected component as policy.generator . no shared base class is needed. saved configuration field names and the checkpoint's cvae.* parameter keys are unchanged. the policy registers its generator under that historical checkpoint name, while callers use generator . existing state dictionaries load strictly without migration. imports use grasppolicy , grasppolicyconfig and build_grasp_policy ; the training cli subcommand is agent:grasp_policy_config . the cvae text point cloud (b, n, 3) -> [yaw canonicalization / augmentation] -> [centering] -> vision encoder (spunet or pointnet) | | | global feature | per-point features | +-> objectness head (target vs background) | +-> graspness head (where to grasp) v cvae encoder (training: ground-truth actions) -> z -> decoder -> (b, n, 3, d) actions d is the hand's joint count for a fixed base; a floating base prepends a translation and a rotation, [xyz, rotation, hand joints] , where the rotation is either euler rxyz or a 6d representation. the three queries are pre-grasp, grasp and post-grasp, in that order. at inference the encoder is skipped: the graspness head picks the top- k points, and the cvae decodes a latent per point — the mean latent when use_mean , otherwise a sample scaled by cvae_temperature . with use_mean the diversity comes from the distinct query points, not the latent. grasp_evaluator_guidance_steps instead refines the latent by ascending a frozen grasp evaluator inside a ball of radius grasp_evaluator_guidance_radius . the vision encoders include a sparse-convolution u-net ( vision_encoder="spconv" , the default, voxel size 5 mm), a bn-free pointnet and rgb cnn/resnet variants. rgb construction and shared training/inference preprocessing live in models/vision_encoder/rgb.py ; the policy keeps state/camera conditioning and generator selection. the cvae is an mlp encoder/decoder over the flattened action vector, conditioned on the vision feature, optionally with a learned prior. flow matching uses the same visual conditioning and action representation. its velocity network is an mlp ( flow ) or transformer ( flow_transformer ), trained along a linear noise-to-action path. sampling integrates eight euler steps and restores physical joint units using the bank's action mean/std. flow returns zero latent moments through the shared training interface, so its kl contribution is zero; joint reconstruction uses mse. losses loss weight field penalizes qpos qpos_weight l1 on the reconstructed hand joints tl , rot tl_weight , rot_weight l1 on floating-base translation and rotation kl kl_weight posterior against the standard or learned prior objectness objectness_weight per-point target-vs-background bce, positives upweighted graspness graspness_weight kl between predicted and labelled graspness distributions kinematic kinematic_weight mse between the fk link positions of predicted and ground-truth actions penetration penetration_weight collision-sphere overlap into the object beyond penetration_threshold , on prior samples prior_fingertip prior_fingertip_weight distance of fingertip spheres to the object surface the last two need scene geometry at training time; the trainer builds it only every penetration_every steps and after penetration_warmup_iters . representation flags convert_rxyz_to_rot6d — 6d rotation inside the cvae, decoded back to euler. analytic_euler picks the closed-form decode over the iterative one. coupled_floating_base — all three queries share the grasp rotation, and grasp and post-grasp share its translation. center_pointcloud — predict translations relative to the cloud centroid. canonical_yaw — rotate into a deterministic yaw frame derived from the cloud's second moment. train_yaw_augmentation — random training-time yaw applied to points and targets together. data graspdataset reads the processed hdf5: per scene, one rendered view is drawn uniformly per access, points are sampled (object-only or whole scene), and actions are sampled per grasp. with graspness enabled, the per-action best points are placed first and the rest sampled around them. graspness labels come from the contact extractor's palm-cone weighting during process_sim_data . fresh flow models use meta/action_mean and meta/action_std to normalize their action space. cvae training uses raw poses. training adamw at lr=1e-4 , weight decay 1e-4 , a 10x step decay two thirds of the way through, ddp when distributed. every step scans the gradients and skips the update if any rank saw a nan or inf. checkpoints hold {"agent": state_dict} ; the provenance keys the benchmark expects ( experiment , policy_config , training ) are added by the packaging scripts. evaluation is described in sim deployment . from prediction to motion a predicted grasp is not executable on its own. grasptrajbuilder applies the filters (hand-axis cone, contact-avoid, penetration, rest pose), optionally ik-converts a floating grasp onto an arm with an orientation gate and an arm-range band, and plans the approach, closing, holding and lift segments. the benchmark runs the filters; deployment skips them and relies on the ik gate, since a real capture has no ground-truth object pose.
graspkit/ref-robot-hands: robot and hand catalog robot and hand catalog every robot is a robotconfig instance in configs/robot/ , registered by name in that package's __init__.py . build_robot_config(name) imports only that module, so only its assets download. hands and rigs name base rig format dof ability_right floating hand urdf 6 allegro_right floating hand urdf 16 barrett_right floating hand urdf 8 dclaw_right floating 3-finger gripper urdf 9 inspire_right floating hand urdf 12 leap_right floating hand urdf 16 mano_right floating hand urdf 16 orca_right floating hand urdf 17 paxini_right floating hand urdf 16 schunk_right floating hand urdf 9 shadow_right , shadow_right_mj floating hand mjcf 22 sharpa_right , sharpa_left floating hand urdf 22 xhand_right , xhand_right_mj floating hand urdf / mjcf 12 robotiq_2f85 , yam_gripper floating gripper urdf 1–2 driven franka_gripper fixed arm + gripper urdf 8 xarm6_sharpa_right fixed arm + hand urdf 6 + 22 xarm7_ability_right fixed arm + hand urdf 7 + 6 xarm7_mano_right fixed arm + hand urdf 7 + 16 xarm7_sharpa_right fixed arm + hand urdf 7 + 22 xarm7_shadow_right fixed arm + hand mjcf 7 + 22 xarm7_xhand_right , xarm7_xhand_right_mj fixed arm + hand urdf / mjcf 7 + 12 g1_inspire_right , g1_inspire_right_wbc fixed humanoid + hand urdf 41 / 33 g1_mano_right fixed humanoid + hand urdf 45 vega_sharpa_right , vega_sharpa_left fixed humanoid + hand urdf full body vega_sharpa_right_mj , vega_sharpa_left_mj fixed humanoid + hand mjcf 63 variants suffixed _side_init and _centered differ only in initial pose or camera framing; _mj variants are the mjcf models used by the mujoco evaluator. not every registered robot has a pipeline: experiments exist for ability, inspire, mano, paxini, sharpa, xhand, the xarm rigs, the g1 rigs, vega and the mujoco shadow. what a config carries paths to the urdf or mjcf, collision spheres, self-collision ignore list, contact points and contact-avoid points; the base type and initial pose; the link names that name the palm, fingertips, thumb and middle finger; and robokit's ee_coord_spec as ee_coord_spec , with the link it is expressed in as ee_coord_link_name . grasp_robot.hand_coord_spec turns it into palm-forward and fingers-up axes in the hand frame (a gripper's jaws are its palm). those axes drive the hand-axis cone filter and the init sampler, so a wrong spec shows up as grasps approaching from the wrong side; tests/test_robot_coord_specs.py checks every config's axes against its fingertips and its sampled inits. contacts come either from a contact-points file or from a contact_candidates_config that samples per link; scripts/tools/create_contact_points.py authors the former. maniskill agents simulation needs a maniskill agent per robot, in mani_skill/agents/ . the uid is the robot config name, with _floating_base appended for floating hands — xhand_right_floating_base , vega_sharpa_right . agents load sim-specific urdfs (floating-base, mimic-free variants) rather than the config's own path, and compose a controller: the six virtual base joints plus a position controller for the fingers. a robot with no hand-written agent (dclaw, orca, paxini, the grippers, every assembled rig) gets one from mani_skill/agents/config_agent.py : register_config_agent builds it from the robot config, writing a mimic-free sim urdf (plus the six virtual base joints for a floating hand) under ~/.graspkit/data/sim_urdf/<revision> . the _mj rigs are mujoco-only. adding a hand write configs/robot/<hand>.py : one robotconfig pointing at the robokit asset symbols. register it in configs/robot/__init__.py . add a maniskill agent in mani_skill/agents/<hand>.py and import it in mani_skill/__init__.py . author contact points if the hand needs them. optionally add it to ees in robokit's assets/robots/assembly/composed.py so it can be mounted on any arm, and to the gallery's hand list. add an experiment config when you want a pipeline for it. configs/robot/schunk.py plus mani_skill/agents/schunk.py is the smallest complete example. assembled rigs robokit's assets/robots/assembly/composed.py assembles any of seven bases (yam, xarm7, xarm6, franka, ur5e, g1, vega) with any of fourteen end effectors, merging collision spheres and computing the mount transform from the two mount specs, on demand under ~/.robokit/assembly/<revision> . utils/assembly_utils.py adds each base's scene placement and rest pose; its configs are what the gallery's arm dropdown offers. a base+ee name is always assembled, even where a hand-written config shares it. uv run python -m graspkit.gallery.grasp_optim --all --gpus ... optimizes every gallery hand floating and jointly on every base, sim-evaluates all of them, and prints the success table.
graspkit/ref-config-system: config system config system all configuration is plain dataclasses in src/graspkit/configs/ , parsed with tyro at the cli. there are no yaml files: experiments are hand-written python instances, variants are derived with dataclasses.replace , and every field is overridable from the command line. field docstrings in the source are authoritative; this page covers the structure and entry points. layout class definitions live in *_config.py ; instances live apart from them. path ( src/graspkit/configs/ ) contents experiment_config.py experimentconfig (top level) and all stage sub-configs experiment/ per-robot experiment instances + name registry ( build_experiment_config , cli_experiment ) robot_config.py robotconfig robot/ per-robot robotconfig instances + name registry ( build_robot_config ) grasp_policy_config.py grasppolicyconfig grasp_policy.py named grasppolicyconfig presets ( grasp_policy_configs ) env_config.py backend configs: msenvconfig (maniskill), mjevalconfig + handspec (mujoco), isaacenvconfig ; the task is envconfig mj_hand.py mujoco handspec instances ( shadow_hand , xhand , ...) real_env_config.py realenvconfig real_env.py realenvconfig hardware presets for realenv ( real_env_configs ; needs the xarm extra) experimentconfig experimentconfig ( experiment_config.py ) is the single config for the whole pipeline ( launch.py and every stage script). sub-configs hold hand-independent algorithm/runtime params; all paths, robot configs, and pipeline control live at the top level. field type role name str experiment name (required) robot_config robotconfig robot that grasp optimization and training target (the floating hand in the standard pipeline) traj_builder grasptrajbuilderconfig floating/fixed robot pair, convert_to_fixed decision, grasp filters, and the builder's motionplannerconfig grasp_optim graspoptimconfig optimizer backend, energy weights, init sampler, in-loop evaluator : see grasp_optim tutorial renderer rendererconfig point-cloud rendering: env, cameras (calibrated extrinsic/intrinsic paths), crop/downsample trainer trainerconfig training loop: batch size, iters, eval envconfig , wandb dataset datasetconfig dataset loading (num actions/points, graspness) agent grasppolicyconfig model architecture/loss preset: see training tutorial scene_description_path , grasp_output_dir , rendered_data_path , processed_data_path , ... str all experiment-specific paths (usually under data_root ) steps , restart_from , append , gpus , num_gpus , seed - pipeline control for launch.py
graspkit/ref-data-format: data format specification data format specification data grasp poses per-scene files one hdf5 file per scene: file name: {scene_id}.h5 datasets (float arrays): grasp_qpos : shape (n, d) pre_grasp_qpos : shape (n, d) post_grasp_qpos : shape (n, d) where: n = number of stored grasps for this scene (varies per scene; may include appended results from multiple runs) d = dimension of the configuration. for floating base robots, this includes 3d position, 3d euler angles (rxyz), and hand joint positions. merged file file name: {output_dir}.h5 structure: one group per scene /{scene_id}/ containing the same datasets as per-scene files
graspkit/ref-assets: graspkit assets graspkit assets data graspkit's own assets (scene descriptions, object-mesh datasets) live in the hf dataset openrobokit/graspkit . robot assets (urdfs, spheres, contact points, self-collision ignores) live in robokit's dataset and are consumed via modules such as robokit.assets.robots.end_effectors.sharpa_hand . import graspkit downloads nothing. a robot module fetches its subtree into ~/.robokit/assets/<pinned-commit>/ ; graspkit assets use ~/.graspkit/assets/<graspkit.assets.revision>/ , fetched by the same robokit.assets.fetch . robotconfig.self_collision_ignore_path points to one robot's ignore yaml. files named *.sphere.yml and *.capsule.yml select the sibling matching the term's representation. grasp optimization defaults to spheres; select spen_representation="capsule" for capsule terms. motion planning and sphere filters always select sphere ignores. an enabled term warns at construction if its matching file is unavailable; an invalid supplied path still raises. runtime assemblies have no ignore path unless one is supplied on their resulting config. layout text calib/ # per-rig camera extrinsics/intrinsics + joint offsets data/scene_description/ # per-task scene msgpacks (dex1b/, ...) data/object_data/ # mesh archives (dex_diffuser*, dexgraspnet, objaverse_dex1b_v2), # extracted at import; dexgraspnet_official_splits/ = train/test lists ~/.graspkit/ : assets/ = fetched hf files (what code reads), hf_cache/ = hf blobs; data/ + logs/ = pipeline output (s3-backed, not assets). data/logs live under home (not the repo), so graspkit works as a library too; graspkit.link() symlinks them into your checkout for browsing. consuming python from graspkit.assets import calib from graspkit.assets.scene_descriptions import dex1b_v0_4 from graspkit.assets.objects import dex_diffuser dex1b_v0_4.floating_mini_path # importing fetches only v0.4 dex_diffuser.data_dir / "processed/ycb" # importing fetches + extracts the archive calib.calib_file("xarm/26-06-21-camera_pose.json") # fetches calib/, returns a path objects are archives: objects.<src> fetches + extracts into data_root/object_data/<src> (marker-guarded) as data_dir ; dexgraspnet_official_splits is archive-free ( dir ). scenes : one module per dex1b version ( _dir = fetch([...], revision, hf_repo_id, graspkit_home) + *_path ). add a scene = add a *_path + its fetch pattern. ad-hoc: robokit.assets.fetch(["data/scene_description/**"], revision, hf_repo_id, graspkit_home) / "..." . bump graspkit.assets.revision after uploading new data. configs/experiments resolve by name, importing only what's needed (so only its assets download): python from graspkit.configs.robot import build_robot_config from graspkit.configs.experiment import build_experiment_config build_robot_config("sharpa_right") # downloads only sharpa_right's robot assets build_experiment_config("sharpa_right_dex1b_v0_4_mini_floating") authoring the dataset is too large to clone, so there's no local git checkout. upload directly through the hf api (uploads only new xet chunks; test mixes in dexdiffuser (egad, kit, contactdb, ycb) as a held-out object family, with per-source counts pinned via merge_scene_description.py 's subsample . tier train test sources dev 100 30 ycb only (train & test) mini 5k 500 train dexgraspnet 684×5; test 300 dexgraspnet test-split + 200 dexdiffuser small 50k 2k train dexgraspnet 4302×5; test dexgraspnet test-split + dexdiffuser families have identical counts/sources (same canonicals, different table). scales: dexgraspnet [0.06, 0.08, 0.1, 0.12, 0.15] , dexdiffuser 1.0 . pipeline: meshes → canonical drop → tabletop randomization , merged with merge_scene_description.py . canonical drop: each (object, scale) is dropped by physics onto a (0.3, 0.3, 0.1) table in 3 orientations ( none , x90 , y90 ). kept if xy within ±0.15m, height ≥ 0.02m, volume ≤ 0.003m³, xy area ≤ 0.025m². tabletop randomization: xy translation and z rotation per canonical scene, plus the family's table pose. height bins: 0.02–0.05, 0.05–0.09, 0.09–0.15, 0.15–0.25m. at most 10 scenes per object (mini), 6 (small), 5 (dev). meshes: collision.glb keeps the coacd convex parts; annealing iterations (warp_gd). each replays one cuda graph; fewer trade grasp quality for speed, and 2000 suits smoke tests.

num_contact_points: int = 4

active contact points per grasp, drawn from the robot's contact candidates; they parameterize the distance and force-closure terms. 4-5 fits most five-finger hands.

switch_possibility: float = 0.5

per-grasp probability, each iteration, of re-drawing the whole contact set; the metropolis test accepts or rejects it together with the pose step.

mu: float = 0.98

rmsprop weight on the current squared gradient, ema = mu * g^2 + (1 - mu) * ema. near 1 the step approaches the gradient's sign times step_size.

step_size: float = 0.005

base rmsprop step; the effective step is step_size * temperature_decay^(t // stepsize_period).

stepsize_period: int = 50

iterations between step-size decays.

starting_temperature: float = 18.0

initial metropolis temperature t: a proposal that worsens the energy by d is still accepted with probability exp(-d / t).

annealing_period: int = 30

iterations per temperature decay, t = starting_temperature * temperature_decay^(t // annealing_period).

temperature_decay: float = 0.95

decay factor shared by the temperature and step-size schedules; closer to 1 cools slower and explores more.

spen_threshold: float = 0.01

self-collision margin (m) between sphere/capsule pairs; 2 cm pinned the middle finger of most hands off the object.

spen_representation: literal['capsule', 'sphere'] = 'sphere'

self-collision geometry for warp_gd: per-link capsules or the collision spheres. warp_lm always uses capsules.

w_fc: float = 1.0

force-closure weight: the active contact normals must balance external wrenches. a zero weight disables any term.

w_dis: float = 100.0

weight pulling each active contact point onto the target surface.

w_fingertip_dis: float = 0.0

weight of the fingertip term (warp_gd only; requires fingertip links set): each fingertip link's closest collision sphere is drawn onto the object. 0 disables; a hand should touch without it, this is a last resort.

w_pen: float = 100.0

warp_gd scene-penetration weight: hand collision spheres against the target and table, with a fixed 5 mm margin. warp_lm uses lm_w_pen.

w_spen: float = 10.0

self-penetration weight between robot links; zero skips building the term.

w_joints: float = 1.0

warp_gd joint-limit weight; q is also clamped to its limits every iteration. warp_lm uses lm_w_joints.

w_angle_z: float = 0.0

weight of the hand-orientation prior (handupangletask, both backends).

angle_z_min: float = math.pi / 2

minimum angle between the hand-up axis and world +z; tabletop configs use it to forbid underhand grasps.

hand_axis: optional[handaxis] = none

hand-axis cone filter on init samples: which hand_coord_spec axis to check, after ik for fixed-base samplers. none disables it. the cone on optimized grasps lives on grasptrajbuilderconfig.

hand_axis_target: tuple[float, float, float] = (0.0, 0.0, 1.0)

filter_hand_axis_max_angle_deg: float = 30.0

hand-axis cone half-angle in degrees.

optimizer_backend: literal['warp_gd', 'warp_lm'] = 'warp_gd'

warp_gd: simulated-annealing gradient descent for floating or fixed-base robots. warp_lm: multi-seed levenberg-marquardt, floating base only, typically 2-3x faster and needs fingertip links; to target an arm, set enable_ik_scoring and let grasptrajbuilder ik-convert.

scene_geom_backend: literal['mesh', 'sdf_volume'] = 'sdf_volume'

sdf_volume: a cached sdf of the target mesh plus analytic table boxes; fast, accuracy bounded by voxel size, and the target must be the scene's only mesh. mesh: per-scene bvhs, exact but slower.

sdf_bake_padding: float = 0.25

sdf bake padding, in mesh units (robokit bakes the unscaled mesh and applies scales at query time).

sdf_resolution: int = 64

voxel grid resolution along the longest axis when sdf_voxel_size is none.

sdf_voxel_size: optional[float] = none

voxel size in mesh units (before scales). none = derive voxel size from sdf_resolution.

lm_w_pen: float = 150.0

lm_w_joints: float = 10.0

warp_lm counterpart of w_joints: position-limit term weight (lm raw-residual scale).

lm_w_fingertip_dis: float = 10.0

warp_lm counterpart of w_fingertip_dis: fingertip-distance term weight (lm raw-residual scale).

lm_collision_margin: float = 0.005

warp_lm scene-collision margin (meters).

lm_residual_eps: float = 1e-06

warp_lm residual epsilon for distance / position-limit / self-penetration terms.

lm_base_step_scale: float = 0.001

warp_lm floating-base step relative to the joint step; keeps base updates from overshooting.

lm_init_sample_range_q: float = 0.2

warp_lm per-seed joint half-range: the 24 seeds are the init qpos plus roberts offsets in [-range, range], clamped to limits.

lm_init_sample_range_base: float = 0.05

warp_lm per-seed base-translation sampling half-range (floating base only).

enable_ik_scoring: bool = false

warp_lm floating base only: oversample inits 16x, keep those an arm ik can reach, and rank solutions by energy plus reachability. use when grasptrajbuilder will ik-convert onto an arm.

evaluator: optional[envconfig] = none

init_ik_orientation_tolerance: float = 0.3

init_rest_pose_max_dist: float = 3.0

graspkit/dev: development guide development guide setup graspkit needs python 3.10–3.14. shell git clone https://github.com/openrobokit/graspkit.git cd graspkit uv sync --extra maniskill --extra spconv uv sync installs the dev and pt-cu126 groups by default; the full pipeline also needs the maniskill and spconv extras (python 3.10–3.12). for another pytorch build, see installation . git workflow create your own branch for development. use pull requests with squash merge to merge to main . delete your branch after merging. github ci runs ruff and the tests on a cpu runner without hugging face access, where tests marked cuda or hf_assets skip, so run the full suite locally on a gpu before opening a pull request. formatting, linting, and tests shell make ci # format + lint + test make format # uvx ruff@0.15.22 format make lint # uvx ruff@0.15.22 check --fix cuda_visible_devices=0 make test # uv run pytest tests tests/ mirrors src/graspkit/ and scripts/ ( tests/scripts/ ), one test<feature> class per feature; shared fixtures live in tests/conftest.py . mark tests that need a gpu with @pytest.mark.cuda and tests that need hugging face assets (robokit robots, graspkit scenes) with @pytest.mark.hf_assets ; import such assets inside the test, since robokit downloads a robot when its module is imported. pre-commit hooks run ruff. pin the same ruff version the makefile does; a newer default rule set reports findings ci does not. running things use uv run , never a bare python or pip . gpu scripts: pick a free gpu first and set cuda_visible_devices . viser scripts serve until interrupted; give them a timeout when scripting them. configs all config classes live in src/graspkit/configs/*_config.py ; their instances live apart, in configs/experiment/ , configs/robot/ , configs/grasp_policy.py , configs/mj_hand.py and configs/real_env.py . a new robot or experiment is a module plus one line in the registry of its package's __init__.py . see the config system . code style type hints on function arguments and return types, except none , any and object . no from __future__ import annotations . prefer fewer, larger functions; add a helper only when it removes real duplication. no try/except, no hasattr , no fallback paths: assume the environment is correct and let the program crash on errors. the robokit boundary robokit holds robot-generic math (terms, solvers, lie, geom, robo); graspkit holds the research pipelines and anything tuned per experiment. code moves to robokit only when a second consumer exists, and it is moved, never copied. robokit is pinned by git rev in pyproject.toml ( [tool.uv.sources] ): to pick up robokit changes, merge there, bump the rev, then uv sync .
